=== 文化財 ===
=== 国宝 ===
; 聖天堂（本殿）
: 拝殿・中殿（相の間）・奥殿からなる廟型式{{jalink|権現造|Q3155268}}（日光東照宮などに見られる、複数棟を一体とした建築形式）の建物である。大工棟梁は妻沼の名工林兵庫正清で幕府作事方棟梁の{{jalink|平内政信|Q11482097}}の子孫に当たり、子の正信の代まで享保20年（1735年）から宝暦10年（1760年）にわたる二十数年をかけて再建されたものである。奥殿は入母屋造、桁行3間・梁間3間、正面向拝付き、中殿は両下造（りょうさげづくり）、桁行3間・梁間1間、拝殿は入母屋造、桁行5間・梁間3間で、これらを接続して1棟とし、屋根はすべて瓦棒銅板葺きとする。
: 奥殿は内外ともに彫刻、漆塗、彩色、金具等を華麗にほどす装飾性の高い建築である。奥殿向拝南面羽目板の「鷲と猿」の彫刻は伝説的な彫刻職人の{{jalink|左甚五郎|Q2668220}}作とも伝承されるが実際の彫刻棟梁は石原吟八郎（吟八）と関口文治郎である。奥殿は柱、長押などの部材に地紋彫をほどこし、内法下の大羽目板には七福神、縁下には唐子遊びを題材とした彩色彫刻をほどこす。彫刻にはそれぞれ中国の故事にちなむ主題が見られ、唐破風下に「三聖吸酸」および「{{jalink|司馬光|Q33566|司馬温公}}の瓶割り」など、拝殿正面唐破風下には「琴棋書画」がある。2003年から2010年にかけて屋根葺き替えと彩色修理を中心とする修理が実施され、当初の彩色がよみがえった。2012年、{{jalink|国宝|Q1139795}}に指定<ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.bunka.go.jp/ima/press_release/pdf/jubunkenzou_shitei_240521.pdf 国宝・重要文化財（建造物）の指定について （文化庁）]}}</ref>{{deadurl|date=2018年7月}}<ref>平成24年度の国宝・重要文化財（建造物）の指定 ○国宝（建造物）より{{Cite book|和書
 |title= 文部科学白書 第8章 第2部／ 文教・科学技術施策の動向と展開ーー文化芸術立国の実現|chapter=平成24年7月9日指定（計1件） 歓喜院 聖天堂 |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/hakusho/html/hpab201301/1338525_019.pdf|format = PDF |page= 294|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2018-07-10}}</ref><ref>平成24年7月9日文部科学省告示第106号</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書|url= http://www.city.kumagaya.lg.jp/kanko/midokoro/menumasyoudenzan/kangiinkokuho.html |title=「歓喜院聖天堂」が国宝に指定|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2012-07-12|publisher= 熊谷市}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|和書|others= 文化財保護委員会; 文化庁文化財保護部 |title = 新指定の文化財 |work= 月刊文化財 |publisher = 第一法規出版 |number= 586|year = 2012|issn= 0016-5948 |ncid= AN00221652}}</ref>。

=== 重要文化財（国指定） ===
[[File:Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|錫杖頭、中心に歓喜天と二童子の像を鋳出す。]]
*貴惣門 - 境内正面入口に位置する高さ18mの銅板葺きの八脚門。屋根を上下二重とし、下重は前後に2つの切妻屋根を架け、側面から見ると3つの破風をもつ特異な形式の門。持国天、多聞天の像を左右に配置している。妻沼の林正道により、嘉永4年竣工、安政2年（1855年）頃の完成。
*錫杖頭（しゃくじょうとう） - 聖天堂の秘仏本尊。建久8年（1197年）の銘があり、中心に歓喜天と二童子の像を鋳出す。錫杖とは、地蔵菩薩などが手に持つ杖のことで、杖の頭部に仏像を表すことがある。

=== 妻沼のいなり寿司 ===
[[ファイル:Menuma Inari-zushi 01.JPG|thumb|200px|妻沼のいなり寿司]]
当院の参拝客を中心として江戸時代から食べられており<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=妻沼のいなり寿司 {{!}} 熊谷観光局|url=https://www.oideyo-kumagaya.com/cate-gourmet/16466/|website=熊谷観光局 {{!}} 熊谷市観光協会公式ホームページ|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>、妻沼地区（旧{{jalink|妻沼町|Q6817684}}）の名物にもなっている{{jalink|稲荷寿司|Q874397}}である。一般的な稲荷寿司とは異なる細長い形状が特徴。
戦前までは、逆にこの細長い形状が一般的だったが、戦後の{{jalink|委託加工制度}}によって、握り寿司のサイズに規格が縮小統一された。しかし、妻沼地域では、細長い形状を維持するよう働きかけが行われた結果、今日まで続く名物寿司となっている<ref>[https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/d0076bcd367b94f88bc134519394ef2463b45486 「ジャンボ」であるために…上申書出し、守った大きさ　熊谷のジャンボいなり「100年フード」認定報告会（埼玉新聞） - Yahoo!ニュース]</ref>。近年では、国宝（本殿）に附随する名物として人気があるとしている<ref name=":0" />。

{{jalink|巻き寿司|Q5739461}}とのセット（助六寿司）を基本として、これを専門に取り扱う3軒の寿司店<ref group="注釈">いずれも当院の門前茶屋として発祥。</ref>が、当院境内や近接地で営業している<ref name=":0" />。また、{{jalink|道の駅めぬま|Q11640968}}の「{{jalink|荻野吟子|Q4794092|吟ぎん}}寿し」など、周辺地域において類似商品が見られる。

{{jalink|農林水産省|Q1376786}}の“うちの郷土料理”サイトでは、当院に由来する「聖天ずし」の名前で紹介されている<ref>{{Cite web|title=聖天ずし 埼玉県 {{!}} うちの郷土料理：農林水産省|url=https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/33_29_saitama.html|website=www.maff.go.jp|access-date=2026-01-17}}</ref>など<ref group="注釈">他に「聖天寿司」とも表記することも。いずれも上記3店のうち境内に面する店舗屋号<!-- 聖天寿し -->の表記ゆれと推定され、3店の統一名称としては不適切と思われる。</ref>、かつては統一した名称は無かったが、熊谷市の観光案内として「'''妻沼のいなり寿司'''」の名称で広報しており<ref>{{Cite web|title=妻沼のいなり寿司 {{!}} 熊谷観光局|url=https://www.oideyo-kumagaya.com/cate-gourmet/16466/|website=熊谷観光局 {{!}} 熊谷市観光協会公式ホームページ|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>、後述の100年フードにもこの名称で応募・登録されていることから、近年では、吟ぎん寿しも含む“妻沼地域の長い稲荷寿司”4店舗各商品<ref name=":0" />の総称として「'''妻沼のいなり寿司'''」と称するのが一般的となっている。

2023年3月3日、{{jalink|文化庁|Q1009519}}『{{jalink|100年フード|Q134383966}}』「伝統の100年フード部門 ～江戸時代から続く郷土の料理～」に認定された<ref>[https://foodculture2021.go.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/r4_100nenfood.pdf 「100年フード」都道府県別一覧（令和４年度）]</ref>。

=== 交通 ===
=== 車 ===
*{{jalink|群馬県道・埼玉県道341号太田熊谷線|Q11609884|県道341号太田熊谷線}}沿い。また、本殿と本坊の間には、{{jalink|埼玉県道59号羽生妻沼線|Q11427072|県道59号羽生妻沼線}}が通っており、「縁結び通り」（当院は縁結びの{{jalink|御利益}}があるとされていることから）と呼ばれる。
*: 周辺に専用駐車場がある。ただし、太田熊谷線 - 貴惣門間の参道に面した駐車スペースおよび、本殿裏手の第6駐車場は参拝客使用不可（公式サイトや現地の案内等を参照のこと）。
*: なお、年始や春・秋大祭時などは混雑するため、熊谷市では南方にある市営めぬま観光駐車場に駐車し、散策しながら参拝することを勧めている。

*{{jalink|朝日自動車|Q11517584|朝日バス}}：{{jalink|熊谷駅|Q735594}}北口6番のりば - [KM61] {{jalink|太田駅 (群馬県)|Q8081729|太田駅}}行・[KM63] {{jalink|西小泉駅|Q11627702}}行・[KM64] 妻沼聖天前行<ref group="注釈">[KM65]妻沼行のバスは「妻沼下町」停留所下車、徒歩13分。</ref>にて、「妻沼聖天前」停留所下車。※ 22時以降の深夜帯は3番のりば発（上記の行先+[KM62] 西矢島行も利用可能）

[[File:Kisoumon.jpg|thumb|240px|Kisoumon]]'''Kangiin'' is {{jalink|Saitama Prefecture|Q128186}}{{jalink|Kumagaya City|Q41106}}{{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684| It is {{jalink|Buddhism|Q748}}{{jalink|temple|Q5393308}} of {{jalink|Koyasan Shingon sect|Q3077357}} located in Menuma}}. {{jalink|Kankiten#Japan's three great holy deities|Q11545315|Japan's three great holy deities}} It is generally referred to as ``Menuma Shodenzan,'' which is a place name attached to the mountain name, and is mainly used in official guides.
Also, "Saitama {{jalink|Nikko Toshogu|Q696641|Nikko}}" (before it was designated as a national treasure, it was "Saitama's Konikko") |publisher= local publisher |isbn= 4-87663-703-2 |date= 2004-09}}</ref> ). It is called ``Shoten-sama (of Menuma)'' by worshipers and local residents.

=== History ===
According to temple legend, in the 3rd year of Jisho ({{jalink|1179|Q19698}}), the military commander {{jalink|Sanemori Saito|Q3472140| It is said that Fujibetsuto Sanemori}} built Shotengu Shrine to enshrine the guardian deity Daisei {{jalink|Kankiten|Q11545315}} (Shoten) and made it the general guardian of Nagaisho. Later, in the 8th year of Kenkyu (1197), Ryo'o Sozu (Sanenaga, the second son of Saito Betto Sanemori) built Kangi-in Choraku-ji Temple as the Betto temple (honbo) of Shotengu Shrine, and it is said that {{jalink|Eleven-faced Kannon|Q11404731}} was the principal image.

{{jalink|Kamakura Shogunate|Q736839}}'s first shogun, {{jalink|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800}}, visited the shrine, and in the medieval period it was protected by the lord of Oshi Castle, and in the early modern period it was rebuilt by {{jalink|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977}}, but it was destroyed by the Great Menuma Fire in 1670. The current Shotendo (main shrine) was rebuilt between the Kyoho and Horeki eras (mid-18th century).

Restoration work on the main shrine was carried out from 2003 to 2011, and the completion ceremony for the main building was held on January 18, 2010, and the completion ceremony was held on June 1, 2011, and it opened to the public on the same day. On July 9, 2012, Seitendo (main shrine) was designated as a {{jalink|National Treasure|Q1139795}} (the first designation as a National Treasure building in Saitama Prefecture).

=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
; Seitendo (main hall)
: It is a mausoleum-style {{jalink|Gongen-zukuri|Q3155268}} building (an architectural style that combines multiple buildings, as seen in Nikko Toshogu Shrine, etc.), which consists of a worship hall, a middle hall (so-ma), and a back hall. The master carpenter was the master carpenter Hayashi Hyogo Masakiyo of Menuma, a descendant of {{jalink|Masanobu Hiranai|Q11482097}}, the master carpenter of the shogunate.The building was rebuilt over a period of more than 20 years, from 1735 to 1760, by his son Masanobu. The inner hall is a gambrel-style structure with 3 girders and 3 girders, with a front facing prayer hall.The middle hall is Ryosage-zukuri, with 3 girder rows and 1 girder.The worship hall is gambrel-style, with 5 girder rows and 3 beams.These are connected to form a single building, and the roof is all roofed with tile-rod copper plates.: The inner and outer halls are highly decorative with splendid carvings, lacquering, coloring, metal fittings, etc. both inside and outside. The ``eagle and monkey'' carvings on the paneling on the south side of the inner hall are said to have been created by the legendary carving craftsman {{jalink|Hidashi Jingoro|Q2668220}}, but the actual master carvers were Ginpachiro Ishihara (Ginpachi) and Bunjiro Sekiguchi. In the inner hall, the pillars, pushpieces, and other members are carved with ground patterns, and the large paneling under the inner law is decorated with the Seven Lucky Gods, and the area under the rim is decorated with colored carvings depicting the theme of playing with karako. Each of the carvings has a theme related to a Chinese story, such as ``Three Saints' Susan'' and ``{{jalink|Sima Guang|Q33566|Sima Wengong}}'s Bottle Breaker'' under the kara gable, and ``Kotogi Calligraphy'' under the kara gable in front of the shrine. Repairs were carried out from 2003 to 2010, mainly re-roofing and coloring, and the original coloring was restored. Designated as {{jalink|National Treasure|Q1139795}} in 2012<ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.bunka.go.jp/ima/press_release/pdf/jubunkenzou_shittei_240521.pdf About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) (Agency for Cultural Affairs)]}}</ref>{{deadurl|date=July 2018}}<ref>Designation of National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties (Buildings) in 2012 ○From National Treasures (Buildings){{Cite book|Japanese book|title= White Paper on Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Chapter 8 Part 2 / Trends and developments in education, science and technology policies - Realizing a nation built on culture and the arts |chapter=Designated on July 9, 2012 (1 item in total) Kangi-in Seitendo |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/hakusho/html/hpab201301/1338525_019.pdf|format = PDF |page= 294|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2018-07-10}}</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 106 of July 9, 2012</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url= http://www.city.kumagaya.lg.jp/kanko/midokoro/menumasyoudenzan/kangiinkokuho.html |title=“Kangi-in Seitendo” designated as a national treasure|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2012-07-12|publisher= Kumagaya City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|Japanese book|others= Cultural Properties Protection Committee; Agency for Cultural Affairs Cultural Properties Protection Department |title = Newly designated cultural properties |work= Monthly cultural properties |publisher = Daiichi Hoki Publishing |number= 586|year = 2012|issn= 0016-5948 |ncid= AN00221652}}</ref>.

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
[[File:Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|The statues of Kangiten and Two Doji are cast in the center. ]]
*Kisomon - An 18m high copper plate roofed eight-legged gate located at the front entrance of the temple grounds. This unique gate has a double roof, upper and lower, with two gable roofs at the front and back, and when viewed from the side, has three gables. Statues of Jikokuten and Tamonten are placed on the left and right. It was built by Masamichi Hayashi of Menuma in the 4th year of the Kaei era, and completed around 1855.
*Shakujoto - The secret principal image of Buddha in Shotendo. There is an inscription dating back to 1197, and the statues of Kangiten and Nidoji are cast in the center. A shakujo is a staff held by Jizo Bodhisattva and others, and the head of the staff sometimes represents a Buddha statue.

=== Inarizushi in Menuma ===
[[File:Menuma Inari-zushi 01.JPG|thumb|200px|Menuma Inari-zushi]]
It has been eaten since the Edo period, mainly by visitors to our hospital. Kumagaya City Tourism Association official website|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, {{jalink|Inari sushi|Q874397}} is a specialty of the Menuma district (formerly {{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684}}). It is characterized by its elongated shape, which is different from typical Inari sushi.Before the war, on the contrary, this elongated shape was common, but after the war, with the {{jalink|contract processing system}}, the standard was reduced to the size of nigiri sushi. However, in the Menuma area, efforts were made to maintain the elongated shape, resulting in the sushi being a specialty that continues to this day. To be a "jumbo"...Submit a report and keep the size Kumagaya's Jumbo Inari "100 Year Food" certification report meeting (Saitama Shimbun) - Yahoo! News]</ref>. In recent years, it has become popular as a specialty attached to the national treasure (main shrine).

{{jalink|Maki sushi|Q5739461}} Three sushi restaurants specialize in this set (Sukeroku sushi), all of which originated as the teahouse in front of our hospital. <ref name=":0" /> operates within the hospital grounds and nearby areas. Similar products can also be found in surrounding areas, such as {{jalink|Roadside Station Menuma|Q11640968}}'s ``{{jalink|Ginko Ogino|Q4794092|Gingin}} Sushi.''On {{jalink|Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|Q1376786}}'s "My Local Cuisine" website, it is introduced under the name "Shoten Sushi", which originates from our hospital.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shoten Sushi Saitama Prefecture {{!}} Our local cuisine: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|url=https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/33_29_saitama.html|website=www.maff.go.jp|access-date=2026-01-17}}</ref> etc.<ref group="Note">It is also sometimes written as "Shoten Sushi". It is presumed that all of these names are misspelled from the shop name <!-- Shoten Sushi --> of the three shops mentioned above, which faces the temple grounds, and it seems inappropriate as a unified name for the three shops. </ref>In the past, there was no unified name, but as a tourist guide for Kumagaya City, it was advertised under the name ``''Menuma no Inarizushi''. Kumagaya City Tourism Association Official Homepage|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, as this name has also been applied and registered in the 100-year food program mentioned below, in recent years, each of the 4 “Nagai Inari Sushi from the Menuma area” products, including Gingin Sushi, have been introduced.<ref name=":0" It is common to refer to the general term ``'''Menuma no Inarizushi''''.March 3, 2023, {{jalink|Agency for Cultural Affairs|Q1009519}} “{{jalink|100 Years of Food|Q134383966}}” “100 Years of Traditional Food Category ～Local cuisine that has continued since the Edo period～” <ref>[https://foodculture2021.go.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/r4_100nenfood.pdf List of “100 Year Food” by prefecture (FY2020)]</ref>.

=== car ===
*{{jalink|Gunma Prefectural Road/Saitama Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line|Q11609884|Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line}} Along. In addition, between the main hall and the main temple, {{jalink|Saitama Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumuma Line|Q11427072|Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumanum Line}} runs, and is called ``Enmusubi Dori'' (because this hospital is said to have {{jalink|divine blessings}} for matchmaking).
*: There is a private parking lot nearby. However, the parking spaces facing the approach between the Ota Kumagaya Line and Kisomon Gate and the 6th parking lot behind the main shrine are not available for use by worshipers (please refer to the official website and local information).
*: Since the shrine is crowded during New Year's holidays and during spring and autumn festivals, Kumagaya City recommends parking at the Menuma Tourist Parking Lot in the south and taking a stroll around the shrine.

=== Bus ===
*{{jalink|Asahi Motors|Q11517584|Asahi Bus}}: {{jalink|Kumagaya Station|Q735594}} North Exit Platform 6 - [KM61] {{jalink|Ota Station (Gunma Prefecture)|Q8081729|Ota Station}} line/[KM63] Take the bus bound for {{jalink|Nishikoizumi Station|Q11627702}}/[KM64] Menuma Shotenmae<ref group="Notes">[KM65] Menuma, get off at the "Menuma Shimomachi" stop, and walk for 13 minutes. </ref>, get off at the "Menuma Shoten-mae" stop. *Late-night hours after 10pm depart from bus stop 3 (destinations above + [KM62] bound for Nishiyajima are also available)
*{{jalink|Yu-Yu Bus (Kumagaya City)|Q11280693|Yu-Yu Bus}} (Community Bus): Glider (Kumagaya Station South Exit - Menuma Administrative Center), Glider Wagon (Menuma Circulation), get off at the "Menuma Shoten-mae" stop or the "Shotenzan Minami Entrance" stop.

[[File:Kisoumon.jpg|thumb|240px|Kisoumon]]'''Kangiin'' is {{jalink|Saitama Prefecture|Q128186}}{{jalink|Kumagaya City|Q41106}}{{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684| It is {{jalink|Buddhism|Q748}}{{jalink|temple|Q5393308}} of {{jalink|Koyasan Shingon sect|Q3077357}} located in Menuma}}. {{jalink|Kankiten#Japan's three great holy deities|Q11545315|Japan's three great holy deities}} It is generally referred to as ``Menuma Shodenzan,'' which is a place name attached to the mountain name, and is mainly used in official guides.
Also, "Saitama {{jalink|Nikko Toshogu|Q696641|Nikko}}" (before it was designated as a national treasure, it was "Saitama's Konikko") |publisher= local publisher |isbn= 4-87663-703-2 |date= 2004-09}}</ref> ). It is called ``Shoten-sama (of Menuma)'' by worshipers and local residents.

=== History ===
According to temple legend, in the 3rd year of Jisho ({{jalink|1179|Q19698}}), the military commander {{jalink|Sanemori Saito|Q3472140| It is said that Fujibetsuto Sanemori}} built Shotengu Shrine to enshrine the guardian deity Daisei {{jalink|Kankiten|Q11545315}} (Shoten) and made it the general guardian of Nagaisho. Later, in the 8th year of Kenkyu (1197), Ryo'o Sozu (Sanenaga, the second son of Saito Betto Sanemori) built Kangi-in Choraku-ji Temple as the Betto temple (honbo) of Shotengu Shrine, and it is said that {{jalink|Eleven-faced Kannon|Q11404731}} was the principal image.

{{jalink|Kamakura Shogunate|Q736839}}'s first shogun, {{jalink|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800}}, visited the shrine, and in the medieval period it was protected by the lord of Oshi Castle, and in the early modern period it was rebuilt by {{jalink|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977}}, but it was destroyed by the Great Menuma Fire in 1670. The current Shotendo (main shrine) was rebuilt between the Kyoho and Horeki eras (mid-18th century).

Restoration work on the main shrine was carried out from 2003 to 2011, and the completion ceremony for the main building was held on January 18, 2010, and the completion ceremony was held on June 1, 2011, and it opened to the public on the same day. On July 9, 2012, Seitendo (main shrine) was designated as a {{jalink|National Treasure|Q1139795}} (the first designation as a National Treasure building in Saitama Prefecture).

=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
; Seitendo (main hall)
: It is a mausoleum-style {{jalink|Gongen-zukuri|Q3155268}} building (an architectural style that combines multiple buildings, as seen in Nikko Toshogu Shrine, etc.), which consists of a worship hall, a middle hall (so-ma), and a back hall. The master carpenter was the master carpenter Hayashi Hyogo Masakiyo of Menuma, a descendant of {{jalink|Masanobu Hiranai|Q11482097}}, the master carpenter of the shogunate.The building was rebuilt over a period of more than 20 years, from 1735 to 1760, by his son Masanobu. The inner hall is a gambrel-style structure with 3 girders and 3 girders, with a front facing prayer hall.The middle hall is Ryosage-zukuri, with 3 girder rows and 1 girder.The worship hall is gambrel-style, with 5 girder rows and 3 beams.These are connected to form a single building, and the roof is all roofed with tile-rod copper plates.: The inner and outer halls are highly decorative with splendid carvings, lacquering, coloring, metal fittings, etc. both inside and outside. The ``eagle and monkey'' carvings on the paneling on the south side of the inner hall are said to have been created by the legendary carving craftsman {{jalink|Hidashi Jingoro|Q2668220}}, but the actual master carvers were Ginpachiro Ishihara (Ginpachi) and Bunjiro Sekiguchi. In the inner hall, the pillars, pushpieces, and other members are carved with ground patterns, and the large paneling under the inner law is decorated with the Seven Lucky Gods, and the area under the rim is decorated with colored carvings depicting the theme of playing with karako. Each of the carvings has a theme related to a Chinese story, such as ``Three Saints' Susan'' and ``{{jalink|Sima Guang|Q33566|Sima Wengong}}'s Bottle Breaker'' under the kara gable, and ``Kotogi Calligraphy'' under the kara gable in front of the shrine. Repairs were carried out from 2003 to 2010, mainly re-roofing and coloring, and the original coloring was restored. Designated as {{jalink|National Treasure|Q1139795}} in 2012<ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.bunka.go.jp/ima/press_release/pdf/jubunkenzou_shittei_240521.pdf About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) (Agency for Cultural Affairs)]}}</ref>{{deadurl|date=July 2018}}<ref>Designation of National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties (Buildings) in 2012 ○From National Treasures (Buildings){{Cite book|Japanese book|title= White Paper on Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Chapter 8 Part 2 / Trends and developments in education, science and technology policies - Realizing a nation built on culture and the arts |chapter=Designated on July 9, 2012 (1 item in total) Kangi-in Seitendo |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/hakusho/html/hpab201301/1338525_019.pdf|format = PDF |page= 294|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2018-07-10}}</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 106 of July 9, 2012</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url= http://www.city.kumagaya.lg.jp/kanko/midokoro/menumasyoudenzan/kangiinkokuho.html |title=“Kangi-in Seitendo” designated as a national treasure|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2012-07-12|publisher= Kumagaya City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|Japanese book|others= Cultural Properties Protection Committee; Agency for Cultural Affairs Cultural Properties Protection Department |title = Newly designated cultural properties |work= Monthly cultural properties |publisher = Daiichi Hoki Publishing |number= 586|year = 2012|issn= 0016-5948 |ncid= AN00221652}}</ref>.

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
[[File:Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|The statues of Kangiten and Two Doji are cast in the center. ]]
*Kisomon - An 18m high copper plate roofed eight-legged gate located at the front entrance of the temple grounds. This unique gate has a double roof, upper and lower, with two gable roofs at the front and back, and when viewed from the side, has three gables. Statues of Jikokuten and Tamonten are placed on the left and right. It was built by Masamichi Hayashi of Menuma in the 4th year of the Kaei era, and completed around 1855.
*Shakujoto - The secret principal image of Buddha in Shotendo. There is an inscription dating back to 1197, and the statues of Kangiten and Nidoji are cast in the center. A shakujo is a staff held by Jizo Bodhisattva and others, and the head of the staff sometimes represents a Buddha statue.

=== Event ===
*Great Ennichidaisai Memorial Service - Held on April 18th and 19th in the spring, and October 18th and 19th in the fall.
*{{jalink|Setsubun|Q746798|Setsubun-kai}} - {{jalink|February 3rd|Q2315}}
*Go's {{jalink|Honinbo#Honinbo Match|Q1197931|Honinbo Match}} - In 2012, the second game of the 67th Honinbo Dogo ({{jalink|Keigo Yamashita|Q2631024}}) vs. {{jalink|Yuta Iyama|Q2982270}} Tengen (the title was the one at the time) was held. Five years later, in 2017, the third game of the 72nd Honinbo Fumihiro (Yuta Iyama) vs. {{jalink|Katsuya Motoki|Q25252413}} 8th Dan was also held.

=== Inarizushi in Menuma ===
[[File:Menuma Inari-zushi 01.JPG|thumb|200px|Menuma Inari-zushi]]
It has been eaten since the Edo period, mainly by visitors to our hospital. Kumagaya City Tourism Association official website|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, {{jalink|Inari sushi|Q874397}} is a specialty of the Menuma district (formerly {{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684}}). It is characterized by its elongated shape, which is different from typical Inari sushi.Before the war, on the contrary, this elongated shape was common, but after the war, with the {{jalink|contract processing system}}, the standard was reduced to the size of nigiri sushi. However, in the Menuma area, efforts were made to maintain the elongated shape, resulting in the sushi being a specialty that continues to this day. To be a "jumbo"...Submit a report and keep the size Kumagaya's Jumbo Inari "100 Year Food" certification report meeting (Saitama Shimbun) - Yahoo! News]</ref>. In recent years, it has become popular as a specialty attached to the national treasure (main shrine).

{{jalink|Maki sushi|Q5739461}} Three sushi restaurants specialize in this set (Sukeroku sushi), all of which originated as the teahouse in front of our hospital. <ref name=":0" /> operates within the hospital grounds and nearby areas. Similar products can also be found in surrounding areas, such as {{jalink|Roadside Station Menuma|Q11640968}}'s ``{{jalink|Ginko Ogino|Q4794092|Gingin}} Sushi.''On {{jalink|Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|Q1376786}}'s "My Local Cuisine" website, it is introduced under the name "Shoten Sushi", which originates from our hospital.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shoten Sushi Saitama Prefecture {{!}} Our local cuisine: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|url=https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/33_29_saitama.html|website=www.maff.go.jp|access-date=2026-01-17}}</ref> etc.<ref group="Note">It is also sometimes written as "Shoten Sushi". It is presumed that all of these names are misspelled from the shop name <!-- Shoten Sushi --> of the three shops mentioned above, which faces the temple grounds, and it seems inappropriate as a unified name for the three shops. </ref>In the past, there was no unified name, but as a tourist guide for Kumagaya City, it was advertised under the name ``''Menuma no Inarizushi''. Kumagaya City Tourism Association Official Homepage|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, as this name has also been applied and registered in the 100-year food program mentioned below, in recent years, each of the 4 “Nagai Inari Sushi from the Menuma area” products, including Gingin Sushi, have been introduced.<ref name=":0" It is common to refer to the general term ``'''Menuma no Inarizushi''''.March 3, 2023, {{jalink|Agency for Cultural Affairs|Q1009519}} “{{jalink|100 Years of Food|Q134383966}}” “100 Years of Traditional Food Category ～Local cuisine that has continued since the Edo period～” <ref>[https://foodculture2021.go.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/r4_100nenfood.pdf List of “100 Year Food” by prefecture (FY2020)]</ref>.

=== Transportation ===

=== car ===
*{{jalink|Gunma Prefectural Road/Saitama Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line|Q11609884|Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line}} Along. In addition, between the main hall and the main temple, {{jalink|Saitama Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumuma Line|Q11427072|Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumanum Line}} runs, and is called ``Enmusubi Dori'' (because this hospital is said to have {{jalink|divine blessings}} for matchmaking).
*: There is a private parking lot nearby. However, the parking spaces facing the approach between the Ota Kumagaya Line and Kisomon Gate and the 6th parking lot behind the main shrine are not available for use by worshipers (please refer to the official website and local information).
*: Since the shrine is crowded during New Year's holidays and during spring and autumn festivals, Kumagaya City recommends parking at the Menuma Tourist Parking Lot in the south and taking a stroll around the shrine.

=== Bus ===
*{{jalink|Asahi Motors|Q11517584|Asahi Bus}}: {{jalink|Kumagaya Station|Q735594}} North Exit Platform 6 - [KM61] {{jalink|Ota Station (Gunma Prefecture)|Q8081729|Ota Station}} line/[KM63] Take the bus bound for {{jalink|Nishikoizumi Station|Q11627702}}/[KM64] Menuma Shotenmae<ref group="Notes">[KM65] Menuma, get off at the "Menuma Shimomachi" stop, and walk for 13 minutes. </ref>, get off at the "Menuma Shoten-mae" stop. *Late-night hours after 10pm depart from bus stop 3 (destinations above + [KM62] bound for Nishiyajima are also available)
*{{jalink|Yu-Yu Bus (Kumagaya City)|Q11280693|Yu-Yu Bus}} (Community Bus): Glider (Kumagaya Station South Exit - Menuma Administrative Center), Glider Wagon (Menuma Circulation), get off at the "Menuma Shoten-mae" stop or the "Shotenzan Minami Entrance" stop.

[[File:Kisoumon.jpg|thumb|240px|Kisoumon]]'''Kangiin'' is {{jalink|Saitama Prefecture|Q128186}}{{jalink|Kumagaya City|Q41106}}{{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684| It is {{jalink|Buddhism|Q748}}{{jalink|temple|Q5393308}} of {{jalink|Koyasan Shingon sect|Q3077357}} located in Menuma}}. {{jalink|Kankiten#Japan's three great holy deities|Q11545315|Japan's three great holy deities}} It is generally referred to as ``Menuma Shodenzan,'' which is a place name attached to the mountain name, and is mainly used in official guides.
Also, "Saitama {{jalink|Nikko Toshogu|Q696641|Nikko}}" (before it was designated as a national treasure, it was "Saitama's Konikko") |publisher= local publisher |isbn= 4-87663-703-2 |date= 2004-09}}</ref> ). It is called ``Shoten-sama (of Menuma)'' by worshipers and local residents.

=== History ===
According to temple legend, in the 3rd year of Jisho ({{jalink|1179|Q19698}}), the military commander {{jalink|Sanemori Saito|Q3472140| It is said that Fujibetsuto Sanemori}} built Shotengu Shrine to enshrine the guardian deity Daisei {{jalink|Kankiten|Q11545315}} (Shoten) and made it the general guardian of Nagaisho. Later, in the 8th year of Kenkyu (1197), Ryo'o Sozu (Sanenaga, the second son of Saito Betto Sanemori) built Kangi-in Choraku-ji Temple as the Betto temple (honbo) of Shotengu Shrine, and it is said that {{jalink|Eleven-faced Kannon|Q11404731}} was the principal image.

{{jalink|Kamakura Shogunate|Q736839}}'s first shogun, {{jalink|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800}}, visited the shrine, and in the medieval period it was protected by the lord of Oshi Castle, and in the early modern period it was rebuilt by {{jalink|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977}}, but it was destroyed by the Great Menuma Fire in 1670. The current Shotendo (main shrine) was rebuilt between the Kyoho and Horeki eras (mid-18th century).

Restoration work on the main shrine was carried out from 2003 to 2011, and the completion ceremony for the main building was held on January 18, 2010, and the completion ceremony was held on June 1, 2011, and it opened to the public on the same day. On July 9, 2012, Seitendo (main shrine) was designated as a {{jalink|National Treasure|Q1139795}} (the first designation as a National Treasure building in Saitama Prefecture).

=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
; Seitendo (main hall)
: It is a mausoleum-style {{jalink|Gongen-zukuri|Q3155268}} building (an architectural style that combines multiple buildings, as seen in Nikko Toshogu Shrine, etc.), which consists of a worship hall, a middle hall (so-ma), and a back hall. The master carpenter was the master carpenter Hayashi Hyogo Masakiyo of Menuma, a descendant of {{jalink|Masanobu Hiranai|Q11482097}}, the master carpenter of the shogunate.The building was rebuilt over a period of more than 20 years, from 1735 to 1760, by his son Masanobu. The inner hall is a gambrel-style structure with 3 girders and 3 girders, with a front facing prayer hall.The middle hall is Ryosage-zukuri, with 3 girder rows and 1 girder.The worship hall is gambrel-style, with 5 girder rows and 3 beams.These are connected to form a single building, and the roof is all roofed with tile-rod copper plates.: The inner and outer halls are highly decorative with splendid carvings, lacquering, coloring, metal fittings, etc. both inside and outside. The ``eagle and monkey'' carvings on the paneling on the south side of the inner hall are said to have been created by the legendary carving craftsman {{jalink|Hidashi Jingoro|Q2668220}}, but the actual master carvers were Ginpachiro Ishihara (Ginpachi) and Bunjiro Sekiguchi. In the inner hall, the pillars, pushpieces, and other members are carved with ground patterns, and the large paneling under the inner law is decorated with the Seven Lucky Gods, and the area under the rim is decorated with colored carvings depicting the theme of playing with karako. Each of the carvings has a theme related to a Chinese story, such as ``Three Saints' Susan'' and ``{{jalink|Sima Guang|Q33566|Sima Wengong}}'s Bottle Breaker'' under the kara gable, and ``Kotogi Calligraphy'' under the kara gable in front of the shrine. Repairs were carried out from 2003 to 2010, mainly re-roofing and coloring, and the original coloring was restored. Designated as {{jalink|National Treasure|Q1139795}} in 2012<ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.bunka.go.jp/ima/press_release/pdf/jubunkenzou_shittei_240521.pdf About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) (Agency for Cultural Affairs)]}}</ref>{{deadurl|date=July 2018}}<ref>Designation of National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties (Buildings) in 2012 ○From National Treasures (Buildings){{Cite book|Japanese book|title= White Paper on Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Chapter 8 Part 2 / Trends and developments in education, science and technology policies - Realizing a nation built on culture and the arts |chapter=Designated on July 9, 2012 (1 item in total) Kangi-in Seitendo |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/hakusho/html/hpab201301/1338525_019.pdf|format = PDF |page= 294|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2018-07-10}}</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 106 of July 9, 2012</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url= http://www.city.kumagaya.lg.jp/kanko/midokoro/menumasyoudenzan/kangiinkokuho.html |title=“Kangi-in Seitendo” designated as a national treasure|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2012-07-12|publisher= Kumagaya City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|Japanese book|others= Cultural Properties Protection Committee; Agency for Cultural Affairs Cultural Properties Protection Department |title = Newly designated cultural properties |work= Monthly cultural properties |publisher = Daiichi Hoki Publishing |number= 586|year = 2012|issn= 0016-5948 |ncid= AN00221652}}</ref>.

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
[[File:Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|The statues of Kangiten and Two Doji are cast in the center. ]]
*Kisomon - An 18m high copper plate roofed eight-legged gate located at the front entrance of the temple grounds. This unique gate has a double roof, upper and lower, with two gable roofs at the front and back, and when viewed from the side, has three gables. Statues of Jikokuten and Tamonten are placed on the left and right. It was built by Masamichi Hayashi of Menuma in the 4th year of the Kaei era, and completed around 1855.
*Shakujoto - The secret principal image of Buddha in Shotendo. There is an inscription dating back to 1197, and the statues of Kangiten and Nidoji are cast in the center. A shakujo is a staff held by Jizo Bodhisattva and others, and the head of the staff sometimes represents a Buddha statue.

=== Inarizushi in Menuma ===
[[File:Menuma Inari-zushi 01.JPG|thumb|200px|Menuma Inari-zushi]]
It has been eaten since the Edo period, mainly by visitors to our hospital. Kumagaya City Tourism Association official website|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, {{jalink|Inari sushi|Q874397}} is a specialty of the Menuma district (formerly {{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684}}). It is characterized by its elongated shape, which is different from typical Inari sushi.Before the war, on the contrary, this elongated shape was common, but after the war, with the {{jalink|contract processing system}}, the standard was reduced to the size of nigiri sushi. However, in the Menuma area, efforts were made to maintain the elongated shape, resulting in the sushi being a specialty that continues to this day. To be a "jumbo"...Submit a report and keep the size Kumagaya's Jumbo Inari "100 Year Food" certification report meeting (Saitama Shimbun) - Yahoo! News]</ref>. In recent years, it has become popular as a specialty attached to the national treasure (main shrine).

{{jalink|Maki sushi|Q5739461}} Three sushi restaurants specialize in this set (Sukeroku sushi), all of which originated as the teahouse in front of our hospital. <ref name=":0" /> operates within the hospital grounds and nearby areas. Similar products can also be found in surrounding areas, such as {{jalink|Roadside Station Menuma|Q11640968}}'s ``{{jalink|Ginko Ogino|Q4794092|Gingin}} Sushi.''On {{jalink|Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|Q1376786}}'s "My Local Cuisine" website, it is introduced under the name "Shoten Sushi", which originates from our hospital.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shoten Sushi Saitama Prefecture {{!}} Our local cuisine: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|url=https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/33_29_saitama.html|website=www.maff.go.jp|access-date=2026-01-17}}</ref> etc.<ref group="Note">It is also sometimes written as "Shoten Sushi". It is presumed that all of these names are misspelled from the shop name <!-- Shoten Sushi --> of the three shops mentioned above, which faces the temple grounds, and it seems inappropriate as a unified name for the three shops. </ref>In the past, there was no unified name, but as a tourist guide for Kumagaya City, it was advertised under the name ``''Menuma no Inarizushi''. Kumagaya City Tourism Association Official Homepage|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, as this name has also been applied and registered in the 100-year food program mentioned below, in recent years, each of the 4 “Nagai Inari Sushi from the Menuma area” products, including Gingin Sushi, have been introduced.<ref name=":0" It is common to refer to the general term ``'''Menuma no Inarizushi''''.March 3, 2023, {{jalink|Agency for Cultural Affairs|Q1009519}} “{{jalink|100 Years of Food|Q134383966}}” “100 Years of Traditional Food Category ～Local cuisine that has continued since the Edo period～” <ref>[https://foodculture2021.go.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/r4_100nenfood.pdf List of “100 Year Food” by prefecture (FY2020)]</ref>.

=== Transportation ===

=== car ===
*{{jalink|Gunma Prefectural Road/Saitama Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line|Q11609884|Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line}} Along. In addition, between the main hall and the main temple, {{jalink|Saitama Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumuma Line|Q11427072|Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumanum Line}} runs, and is called ``Enmusubi Dori'' (because this hospital is said to have {{jalink|divine blessings}} for matchmaking).
*: There is a private parking lot nearby. However, the parking spaces facing the approach between the Ota Kumagaya Line and Kisomon Gate and the 6th parking lot behind the main shrine are not available for use by worshipers (please refer to the official website and local information).
*: Since the shrine is crowded during New Year's holidays and during spring and autumn festivals, Kumagaya City recommends parking at the Menuma Tourist Parking Lot in the south and taking a stroll around the shrine.

[[File:Kisoumon.jpg|thumb|240px|Kisoumon]]'''Kangiin'' is {{jalink|Saitama Prefecture|Q128186}}{{jalink|Kumagaya City|Q41106}}{{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684| It is {{jalink|Buddhism|Q748}}{{jalink|temple|Q5393308}} of {{jalink|Koyasan Shingon sect|Q3077357}} located in Menuma}}. {{jalink|Kankiten#Japan's three great holy deities|Q11545315|Japan's three great holy deities}} It is generally referred to as ``Menuma Shodenzan,'' which is a place name attached to the mountain name, and is mainly used in official guides.
Also, "Saitama {{jalink|Nikko Toshogu|Q696641|Nikko}}" (before it was designated as a national treasure, it was "Saitama's Konikko") |publisher= local publisher |isbn= 4-87663-703-2 |date= 2004-09}}</ref> ). It is called ``Shoten-sama (of Menuma)'' by worshipers and local residents.

=== History ===
According to temple legend, in the 3rd year of Jisho ({{jalink|1179|Q19698}}), the military commander {{jalink|Sanemori Saito|Q3472140| It is said that Fujibetsuto Sanemori}} built Shotengu Shrine to enshrine the guardian deity Daisei {{jalink|Kankiten|Q11545315}} (Shoten) and made it the general guardian of Nagaisho. Later, in the 8th year of Kenkyu (1197), Ryo'o Sozu (Sanenaga, the second son of Saito Betto Sanemori) built Kangi-in Choraku-ji Temple as the Betto temple (honbo) of Shotengu Shrine, and it is said that {{jalink|Eleven-faced Kannon|Q11404731}} was the principal image.

{{jalink|Kamakura Shogunate|Q736839}}'s first shogun, {{jalink|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800}}, visited the shrine, and in the medieval period it was protected by the lord of Oshi Castle, and in the early modern period it was rebuilt by {{jalink|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977}}, but it was destroyed by the Great Menuma Fire in 1670. The current Shotendo (main shrine) was rebuilt between the Kyoho and Horeki eras (mid-18th century).

Restoration work on the main shrine was carried out from 2003 to 2011, and the completion ceremony for the main building was held on January 18, 2010, and the completion ceremony was held on June 1, 2011, and it opened to the public on the same day. On July 9, 2012, Seitendo (main shrine) was designated as a {{jalink|National Treasure|Q1139795}} (the first designation as a National Treasure building in Saitama Prefecture).

=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
; Seitendo (main hall)
: It is a mausoleum-style {{jalink|Gongen-zukuri|Q3155268}} building (an architectural style that combines multiple buildings, as seen in Nikko Toshogu Shrine, etc.), which consists of a worship hall, a middle hall (so-ma), and a back hall. The master carpenter was the master carpenter Hayashi Hyogo Masakiyo of Menuma, a descendant of {{jalink|Masanobu Hiranai|Q11482097}}, the master carpenter of the shogunate.The building was rebuilt over a period of more than 20 years, from 1735 to 1760, by his son Masanobu. The inner hall is a gambrel-style structure with 3 girders and 3 girders, with a front facing prayer hall.The middle hall is Ryosage-zukuri, with 3 girder rows and 1 girder.The worship hall is gambrel-style, with 5 girder rows and 3 beams.These are connected to form a single building, and the roof is all roofed with tile-rod copper plates.: The inner and outer halls are highly decorative with splendid carvings, lacquering, coloring, metal fittings, etc. both inside and outside. The ``eagle and monkey'' carvings on the paneling on the south side of the inner hall are said to have been created by the legendary carving craftsman {{jalink|Hidashi Jingoro|Q2668220}}, but the actual master carvers were Ginpachiro Ishihara (Ginpachi) and Bunjiro Sekiguchi. In the inner hall, the pillars, pushpieces, and other members are carved with ground patterns, and the large paneling under the inner law is decorated with the Seven Lucky Gods, and the area under the rim is decorated with colored carvings depicting the theme of playing with karako. Each of the carvings has a theme related to a Chinese story, such as ``Three Saints' Susan'' and ``{{jalink|Sima Guang|Q33566|Sima Wengong}}'s Bottle Breaker'' under the kara gable, and ``Kotogi Calligraphy'' under the kara gable in front of the shrine. Repairs were carried out from 2003 to 2010, mainly re-roofing and coloring, and the original coloring was restored. Designated as {{jalink|National Treasure|Q1139795}} in 2012<ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.bunka.go.jp/ima/press_release/pdf/jubunkenzou_shittei_240521.pdf About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) (Agency for Cultural Affairs)]}}</ref>{{deadurl|date=July 2018}}<ref>Designation of National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties (Buildings) in 2012 ○From National Treasures (Buildings){{Cite book|Japanese book|title= White Paper on Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Chapter 8 Part 2 / Trends and developments in education, science and technology policies - Realizing a nation built on culture and the arts |chapter=Designated on July 9, 2012 (1 item in total) Kangi-in Seitendo |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/hakusho/html/hpab201301/1338525_019.pdf|format = PDF |page= 294|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2018-07-10}}</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 106 of July 9, 2012</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url= http://www.city.kumagaya.lg.jp/kanko/midokoro/menumasyoudenzan/kangiinkokuho.html |title=“Kangi-in Seitendo” designated as a national treasure|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2012-07-12|publisher= Kumagaya City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|Japanese book|others= Cultural Properties Protection Committee; Agency for Cultural Affairs Cultural Properties Protection Department |title = Newly designated cultural properties |work= Monthly cultural properties |publisher = Daiichi Hoki Publishing |number= 586|year = 2012|issn= 0016-5948 |ncid= AN00221652}}</ref>.

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
[[File:Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|The statues of Kangiten and Two Doji are cast in the center. ]]
*Kisomon - An 18m high copper plate roofed eight-legged gate located at the front entrance of the temple grounds. This unique gate has a double roof, upper and lower, with two gable roofs at the front and back, and when viewed from the side, has three gables. Statues of Jikokuten and Tamonten are placed on the left and right. It was built by Masamichi Hayashi of Menuma in the 4th year of the Kaei era, and completed around 1855.
*Shakujoto - The secret principal image of Buddha in Shotendo. There is an inscription dating back to 1197, and the statues of Kangiten and Nidoji are cast in the center. A shakujo is a staff held by Jizo Bodhisattva and others, and the head of the staff sometimes represents a Buddha statue.

=== Inarizushi in Menuma ===
[[File:Menuma Inari-zushi 01.JPG|thumb|200px|Menuma Inari-zushi]]
It has been eaten since the Edo period, mainly by visitors to our hospital. Kumagaya City Tourism Association official website|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, {{jalink|Inari sushi|Q874397}} is a specialty of the Menuma district (formerly {{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684}}). It is characterized by its elongated shape, which is different from typical Inari sushi.Before the war, on the contrary, this elongated shape was common, but after the war, with the {{jalink|contract processing system}}, the standard was reduced to the size of nigiri sushi. However, in the Menuma area, efforts were made to maintain the elongated shape, resulting in the sushi being a specialty that continues to this day. To be a "jumbo"...Submit a report and keep the size Kumagaya's Jumbo Inari "100 Year Food" certification report meeting (Saitama Shimbun) - Yahoo! News]</ref>. In recent years, it has become popular as a specialty attached to the national treasure (main shrine).

{{jalink|Maki sushi|Q5739461}} Three sushi restaurants specialize in this set (Sukeroku sushi), all of which originated as the teahouse in front of our hospital. <ref name=":0" /> operates within the hospital grounds and nearby areas. Similar products can also be found in surrounding areas, such as {{jalink|Roadside Station Menuma|Q11640968}}'s ``{{jalink|Ginko Ogino|Q4794092|Gingin}} Sushi.''On {{jalink|Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|Q1376786}}'s "My Local Cuisine" website, it is introduced under the name "Shoten Sushi", which originates from our hospital.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shoten Sushi Saitama Prefecture {{!}} Our local cuisine: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|url=https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/33_29_saitama.html|website=www.maff.go.jp|access-date=2026-01-17}}</ref> etc.<ref group="Note">It is also sometimes written as "Shoten Sushi". It is presumed that all of these names are misspelled from the shop name <!-- Shoten Sushi --> of the three shops mentioned above, which faces the temple grounds, and it seems inappropriate as a unified name for the three shops. </ref>In the past, there was no unified name, but as a tourist guide for Kumagaya City, it was advertised under the name ``''Menuma no Inarizushi''. Kumagaya City Tourism Association Official Homepage|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, as this name has also been applied and registered in the 100-year food program mentioned below, in recent years, each of the 4 “Nagai Inari Sushi from the Menuma area” products, including Gingin Sushi, have been introduced.<ref name=":0" It is common to refer to the general term ``'''Menuma no Inarizushi''''.March 3, 2023, {{jalink|Agency for Cultural Affairs|Q1009519}} “{{jalink|100 Years of Food|Q134383966}}” “100 Years of Traditional Food Category ～Local cuisine that has continued since the Edo period～” <ref>[https://foodculture2021.go.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/r4_100nenfood.pdf List of “100 Year Food” by prefecture (FY2020)]</ref>.

=== Transportation ===

=== car ===
*{{jalink|Gunma Prefectural Road/Saitama Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line|Q11609884|Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line}} Along. In addition, between the main hall and the main temple, {{jalink|Saitama Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumuma Line|Q11427072|Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumanum Line}} runs, and is called ``Enmusubi Dori'' (because this hospital is said to have {{jalink|divine blessings}} for matchmaking).
*: There is a private parking lot nearby. However, the parking spaces facing the approach between the Ota Kumagaya Line and Kisomon Gate and the 6th parking lot behind the main shrine are not available for use by worshipers (please refer to the official website and local information).
*: Since the shrine is crowded during New Year's holidays and during spring and autumn festivals, Kumagaya City recommends parking at the Menuma Tourist Parking Lot in the south and taking a stroll around the shrine.

=== Bus ===
*{{jalink|Asahi Motors|Q11517584|Asahi Bus}}: {{jalink|Kumagaya Station|Q735594}} North Exit Platform 6 - [KM61] {{jalink|Ota Station (Gunma Prefecture)|Q8081729|Ota Station}} line/[KM63] Take the bus bound for {{jalink|Nishikoizumi Station|Q11627702}}/[KM64] Menuma Shotenmae<ref group="Notes">[KM65] Menuma, get off at the "Menuma Shimomachi" stop, and walk for 13 minutes. </ref>, get off at the "Menuma Shoten-mae" stop. *Late-night hours after 10pm depart from bus stop 3 (destinations above + [KM62] bound for Nishiyajima are also available)
*{{jalink|Yu-Yu Bus (Kumagaya City)|Q11280693|Yu-Yu Bus}} (Community Bus): Glider (Kumagaya Station South Exit - Menuma Administrative Center), Glider Wagon (Menuma Circulation), get off at the "Menuma Shoten-mae" stop or the "Shotenzan Minami Entrance" stop.

[[File:Kisoumon.jpg|thumb|240px|Kisoumon]]'''Kangiin'' is {{jalink|Saitama Prefecture|Q128186}}{{jalink|Kumagaya City|Q41106}}{{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684| It is {{jalink|Buddhism|Q748}}{{jalink|temple|Q5393308}} of {{jalink|Koyasan Shingon sect|Q3077357}} located in Menuma}}. {{jalink|Kankiten#Japan's three great holy deities|Q11545315|Japan's three great holy deities}} It is generally referred to as ``Menuma Shodenzan,'' which is a place name attached to the mountain name, and is mainly used in official guides.
Also, "Saitama {{jalink|Nikko Toshogu|Q696641|Nikko}}" (before it was designated as a national treasure, it was "Saitama's Konikko") |publisher= local publisher |isbn= 4-87663-703-2 |date= 2004-09}}</ref> ). It is called ``Shoten-sama (of Menuma)'' by worshipers and local residents.

=== History ===
According to temple legend, in the 3rd year of Jisho ({{jalink|1179|Q19698}}), the military commander {{jalink|Sanemori Saito|Q3472140| It is said that Fujibetsuto Sanemori}} built Shotengu Shrine to enshrine the guardian deity Daisei {{jalink|Kankiten|Q11545315}} (Shoten) and made it the general guardian of Nagaisho. Later, in the 8th year of Kenkyu (1197), Ryo'o Sozu (Sanenaga, the second son of Saito Betto Sanemori) built Kangi-in Choraku-ji Temple as the Betto temple (honbo) of Shotengu Shrine, and it is said that {{jalink|Eleven-faced Kannon|Q11404731}} was the principal image.

{{jalink|Kamakura Shogunate|Q736839}}'s first shogun, {{jalink|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800}}, visited the shrine, and in the medieval period it was protected by the lord of Oshi Castle, and in the early modern period it was rebuilt by {{jalink|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977}}, but it was destroyed by the Great Menuma Fire in 1670. The current Shotendo (main shrine) was rebuilt between the Kyoho and Horeki eras (mid-18th century).

Restoration work on the main shrine was carried out from 2003 to 2011, and the completion ceremony for the main building was held on January 18, 2010, and the completion ceremony was held on June 1, 2011, and it opened to the public on the same day. On July 9, 2012, Seitendo (main shrine) was designated as a {{jalink|National Treasure|Q1139795}} (the first designation as a National Treasure building in Saitama Prefecture).

=== Precincts ===
<!--Introduced on the official website-->
*Main shrine (Shotendo)
*: Restoration work from 2003 to 2011 brought back the brightly colored carvings from when the building was first built. The total construction cost was 1.35 billion yen. 960 million yen came from national, prefectural and city subsidies, and 350 million yen came from donations from believers.
*: An admission fee of 700 yen is required to visit the inner shrine (no admission fee is required for regular visits to the shrine).
*Daishido
*:{{jalink|Eighty-eight Kanto locations|Q11655881}} No. 88 prayer hall.
*Niomon

=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
; Seitendo (main hall)
: It is a mausoleum-style {{jalink|Gongen-zukuri|Q3155268}} building (an architectural style that combines multiple buildings, as seen in Nikko Toshogu Shrine, etc.), which consists of a worship hall, a middle hall (so-ma), and a back hall. The master carpenter was the master carpenter Hayashi Hyogo Masakiyo of Menuma, a descendant of {{jalink|Masanobu Hiranai|Q11482097}}, the master carpenter of the shogunate.The building was rebuilt over a period of more than 20 years, from 1735 to 1760, by his son Masanobu. The inner hall is a gambrel-style structure with 3 girders and 3 girders, with a front facing prayer hall.The middle hall is Ryosage-zukuri, with 3 girder rows and 1 girder.The worship hall is gambrel-style, with 5 girder rows and 3 beams.These are connected to form a single building, and the roof is all roofed with tile-rod copper plates.: The inner and outer halls are highly decorative with splendid carvings, lacquering, coloring, metal fittings, etc. both inside and outside. The ``eagle and monkey'' carvings on the paneling on the south side of the inner hall are said to have been created by the legendary carving craftsman {{jalink|Hidashi Jingoro|Q2668220}}, but the actual master carvers were Ginpachiro Ishihara (Ginpachi) and Bunjiro Sekiguchi. In the inner hall, the pillars, pushpieces, and other members are carved with ground patterns, and the large paneling under the inner law is decorated with the Seven Lucky Gods, and the area under the rim is decorated with colored carvings depicting the theme of playing with karako. Each of the carvings has a theme related to a Chinese story, such as ``Three Saints' Susan'' and ``{{jalink|Sima Guang|Q33566|Sima Wengong}}'s Bottle Breaker'' under the kara gable, and ``Kotogi Calligraphy'' under the kara gable in front of the shrine. Repairs were carried out from 2003 to 2010, mainly re-roofing and coloring, and the original coloring was restored. Designated as {{jalink|National Treasure|Q1139795}} in 2012<ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.bunka.go.jp/ima/press_release/pdf/jubunkenzou_shittei_240521.pdf About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) (Agency for Cultural Affairs)]}}</ref>{{deadurl|date=July 2018}}<ref>Designation of National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties (Buildings) in 2012 ○From National Treasures (Buildings){{Cite book|Japanese book|title= White Paper on Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Chapter 8 Part 2 / Trends and developments in education, science and technology policies - Realizing a nation built on culture and the arts |chapter=Designated on July 9, 2012 (1 item in total) Kangi-in Seitendo |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/hakusho/html/hpab201301/1338525_019.pdf|format = PDF |page= 294|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2018-07-10}}</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 106 of July 9, 2012</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url= http://www.city.kumagaya.lg.jp/kanko/midokoro/menumasyoudenzan/kangiinkokuho.html |title=“Kangi-in Seitendo” designated as a national treasure|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2012-07-12|publisher= Kumagaya City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|Japanese book|others= Cultural Properties Protection Committee; Agency for Cultural Affairs Cultural Properties Protection Department |title = Newly designated cultural properties |work= Monthly cultural properties |publisher = Daiichi Hoki Publishing |number= 586|year = 2012|issn= 0016-5948 |ncid= AN00221652}}</ref>.

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
[[File:Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|The statues of Kangiten and Two Doji are cast in the center. ]]
*Kisomon - An 18m high copper plate roofed eight-legged gate located at the front entrance of the temple grounds. This unique gate has a double roof, upper and lower, with two gable roofs at the front and back, and when viewed from the side, has three gables. Statues of Jikokuten and Tamonten are placed on the left and right. It was built by Masamichi Hayashi of Menuma in the 4th year of the Kaei era, and completed around 1855.
*Shakujoto - The secret principal image of Buddha in Shotendo. There is an inscription dating back to 1197, and the statues of Kangiten and Nidoji are cast in the center. A shakujo is a staff held by Jizo Bodhisattva and others, and the head of the staff sometimes represents a Buddha statue.

=== Inarizushi in Menuma ===
[[File:Menuma Inari-zushi 01.JPG|thumb|200px|Menuma Inari-zushi]]
It has been eaten since the Edo period, mainly by visitors to our hospital. Kumagaya City Tourism Association official website|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, {{jalink|Inari sushi|Q874397}} is a specialty of the Menuma district (formerly {{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684}}). It is characterized by its elongated shape, which is different from typical Inari sushi.Before the war, on the contrary, this elongated shape was common, but after the war, with the {{jalink|contract processing system}}, the standard was reduced to the size of nigiri sushi. However, in the Menuma area, efforts were made to maintain the elongated shape, resulting in the sushi being a specialty that continues to this day. To be a "jumbo"...Submit a report and keep the size Kumagaya's Jumbo Inari "100 Year Food" certification report meeting (Saitama Shimbun) - Yahoo! News]</ref>. In recent years, it has become popular as a specialty attached to the national treasure (main shrine).

{{jalink|Maki sushi|Q5739461}} Three sushi restaurants specialize in this set (Sukeroku sushi), all of which originated as the teahouse in front of our hospital. <ref name=":0" /> operates within the hospital grounds and nearby areas. Similar products can also be found in surrounding areas, such as {{jalink|Roadside Station Menuma|Q11640968}}'s ``{{jalink|Ginko Ogino|Q4794092|Gingin}} Sushi.''On {{jalink|Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|Q1376786}}'s "My Local Cuisine" website, it is introduced under the name "Shoten Sushi", which originates from our hospital.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shoten Sushi Saitama Prefecture {{!}} Our local cuisine: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|url=https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/33_29_saitama.html|website=www.maff.go.jp|access-date=2026-01-17}}</ref> etc.<ref group="Note">It is also sometimes written as "Shoten Sushi". It is presumed that all of these names are misspelled from the shop name <!-- Shoten Sushi --> of the three shops mentioned above, which faces the temple grounds, and it seems inappropriate as a unified name for the three shops. </ref>In the past, there was no unified name, but as a tourist guide for Kumagaya City, it was advertised under the name ``''Menuma no Inarizushi''. Kumagaya City Tourism Association Official Homepage|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, as this name has also been applied and registered in the 100-year food program mentioned below, in recent years, each of the 4 “Nagai Inari Sushi from the Menuma area” products, including Gingin Sushi, have been introduced.<ref name=":0" It is common to refer to the general term ``'''Menuma no Inarizushi''''.March 3, 2023, {{jalink|Agency for Cultural Affairs|Q1009519}} “{{jalink|100 Years of Food|Q134383966}}” “100 Years of Traditional Food Category ～Local cuisine that has continued since the Edo period～” <ref>[https://foodculture2021.go.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/r4_100nenfood.pdf List of “100 Year Food” by prefecture (FY2020)]</ref>.

=== Transportation ===

=== car ===
*{{jalink|Gunma Prefectural Road/Saitama Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line|Q11609884|Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line}} Along. In addition, between the main hall and the main temple, {{jalink|Saitama Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumuma Line|Q11427072|Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumanum Line}} runs, and is called ``Enmusubi Dori'' (because this hospital is said to have {{jalink|divine blessings}} for matchmaking).
*: There is a private parking lot nearby. However, the parking spaces facing the approach between the Ota Kumagaya Line and Kisomon Gate and the 6th parking lot behind the main shrine are not available for use by worshipers (please refer to the official website and local information).
*: Since the shrine is crowded during New Year's holidays and during spring and autumn festivals, Kumagaya City recommends parking at the Menuma Tourist Parking Lot in the south and taking a stroll around the shrine.

[[File:Kisoumon.jpg|thumb|240px|Kisoumon]]'''Kangiin'' is {{ill|lt=Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|WD=Q128186}}{{ill|lt=Kumagaya City|Q41106|WD=Q41106}}{{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684| It is {{ill|lt=Buddhism|Q748|WD=Q748}}{{ill|lt=temple|Q5393308|WD=Q5393308}} of {{ill|lt=Koyasan Shingon sect|Q3077357|WD=Q3077357}} located in Menuma}}. {{ill|lt=Kankiten#Japan's three great holy deities|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315|lt=Japan's three great holy deities}} It is generally referred to as ``Menuma Shodenzan,'' which is a place name attached to the mountain name, and is mainly used in official guides.
Also, "Saitama {{ill|lt=Nikko Toshogu|Q696641|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikko}}" (before it was designated as a national treasure, it was "Saitama's Konikko") |publisher= local publisher |isbn= 4-87663-703-2 |date= 2004-09}}</ref> ). It is called ``Shoten-sama (of Menuma)'' by worshipers and local residents.

=== History ===
According to temple legend, in the 3rd year of Jisho ({{ill|lt=1179|Q19698|WD=Q19698}}), the military commander {{ill|lt=Sanemori Saito|Q3472140|WD=Q3472140|lt=It is said that Fujibetsuto Sanemori}} built Shotengu Shrine to enshrine the guardian deity Daisei {{ill|lt=Kankiten|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315}} (Shoten) and made it the general guardian of Nagaisho. Later, in the 8th year of Kenkyu (1197), Ryo'o Sozu (Sanenaga, the second son of Saito Betto Sanemori) built Kangi-in Choraku-ji Temple as the Betto temple (honbo) of Shotengu Shrine, and it is said that {{ill|lt=Eleven-faced Kannon|Q11404731|WD=Q11404731}} was the principal image.

{{ill|lt=Kamakura Shogunate|Q736839|WD=Q736839}}'s first shogun, {{ill|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|WD=Q242800}}, visited the shrine, and in the medieval period it was protected by the lord of Oshi Castle, and in the early modern period it was rebuilt by {{ill|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|WD=Q171977}}, but it was destroyed by the Great Menuma Fire in 1670. The current Shotendo (main shrine) was rebuilt between the Kyoho and Horeki eras (mid-18th century).

Restoration work on the main shrine was carried out from 2003 to 2011, and the completion ceremony for the main building was held on January 18, 2010, and the completion ceremony was held on June 1, 2011, and it opened to the public on the same day. On July 9, 2012, Seitendo (main shrine) was designated as a {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795}} (the first designation as a National Treasure building in Saitama Prefecture).

=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
; Seitendo (main hall)
: It is a mausoleum-style {{ill|lt=Gongen-zukuri|Q3155268|WD=Q3155268}} building (an architectural style that combines multiple buildings, as seen in Nikko Toshogu Shrine, etc.), which consists of a worship hall, a middle hall (so-ma), and a back hall. The master carpenter was the master carpenter Hayashi Hyogo Masakiyo of Menuma, a descendant of {{ill|lt=Masanobu Hiranai|Q11482097|WD=Q11482097}}, the master carpenter of the shogunate.The building was rebuilt over a period of more than 20 years, from 1735 to 1760, by his son Masanobu. The inner hall is a gambrel-style structure with 3 girders and 3 girders, with a front facing prayer hall.The middle hall is Ryosage-zukuri, with 3 girder rows and 1 girder.The worship hall is gambrel-style, with 5 girder rows and 3 beams.These are connected to form a single building, and the roof is all roofed with tile-rod copper plates.: The inner and outer halls are highly decorative with splendid carvings, lacquering, coloring, metal fittings, etc. both inside and outside. The ``eagle and monkey'' carvings on the paneling on the south side of the inner hall are said to have been created by the legendary carving craftsman {{ill|lt=Hidashi Jingoro|Q2668220|WD=Q2668220}}, but the actual master carvers were Ginpachiro Ishihara (Ginpachi) and Bunjiro Sekiguchi. In the inner hall, the pillars, pushpieces, and other members are carved with ground patterns, and the large paneling under the inner law is decorated with the Seven Lucky Gods, and the area under the rim is decorated with colored carvings depicting the theme of playing with karako. Each of the carvings has a theme related to a Chinese story, such as ``Three Saints' Susan'' and ``{{ill|lt=Sima Guang|Q33566|WD=Q33566|lt=Sima Wengong}}'s Bottle Breaker'' under the kara gable, and ``Kotogi Calligraphy'' under the kara gable in front of the shrine. Repairs were carried out from 2003 to 2010, mainly re-roofing and coloring, and the original coloring was restored. Designated as {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795}} in 2012<ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.bunka.go.jp/ima/press_release/pdf/jubunkenzou_shittei_240521.pdf About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) (Agency for Cultural Affairs)]}}</ref>{{deadurl|date=July 2018}}<ref>Designation of National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties (Buildings) in 2012 ○From National Treasures (Buildings){{Cite book|Japanese book|title= White Paper on Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Chapter 8 Part 2 / Trends and developments in education, science and technology policies - Realizing a nation built on culture and the arts |chapter=Designated on July 9, 2012 (1 item in total) Kangi-in Seitendo |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/hakusho/html/hpab201301/1338525_019.pdf|format = PDF |page= 294|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2018-07-10}}</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 106 of July 9, 2012</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url= http://www.city.kumagaya.lg.jp/kanko/midokoro/menumasyoudenzan/kangiinkokuho.html |title=“Kangi-in Seitendo” designated as a national treasure|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2012-07-12|publisher= Kumagaya City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|Japanese book|others= Cultural Properties Protection Committee; Agency for Cultural Affairs Cultural Properties Protection Department |title = Newly designated cultural properties |work= Monthly cultural properties |publisher = Daiichi Hoki Publishing |number= 586|year = 2012|issn= 0016-5948 |ncid= AN00221652}}</ref>.

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
[[File:Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|The statues of Kangiten and Two Doji are cast in the center. ]]
*Kisomon - An 18m high copper plate roofed eight-legged gate located at the front entrance of the temple grounds. This unique gate has a double roof, upper and lower, with two gable roofs at the front and back, and when viewed from the side, has three gables. Statues of Jikokuten and Tamonten are placed on the left and right. It was built by Masamichi Hayashi of Menuma in the 4th year of the Kaei era, and completed around 1855.
*Shakujoto - The secret principal image of Buddha in Shotendo. There is an inscription dating back to 1197, and the statues of Kangiten and Nidoji are cast in the center. A shakujo is a staff held by Jizo Bodhisattva and others, and the head of the staff sometimes represents a Buddha statue.

=== Inarizushi in Menuma ===
[[File:Menuma Inari-zushi 01.JPG|thumb|200px|Menuma Inari-zushi]]
It has been eaten since the Edo period, mainly by visitors to our hospital. Kumagaya City Tourism Association official website|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, {{ill|lt=Inari sushi|Q874397|WD=Q874397}} is a specialty of the Menuma district (formerly {{ill|lt=Menuma Town|Q6817684|WD=Q6817684}}). It is characterized by its elongated shape, which is different from typical Inari sushi.Before the war, on the contrary, this elongated shape was common, but after the war, with the {{ill||lt=contract processing system|UNKNOWN}}, the standard was reduced to the size of nigiri sushi. However, in the Menuma area, efforts were made to maintain the elongated shape, resulting in the sushi being a specialty that continues to this day. To be a "jumbo"...Submit a report and keep the size Kumagaya's Jumbo Inari "100 Year Food" certification report meeting (Saitama Shimbun) - Yahoo! News]</ref>. In recent years, it has become popular as a specialty attached to the national treasure (main shrine).

{{ill|lt=Maki sushi|Q5739461|WD=Q5739461}} Three sushi restaurants specialize in this set (Sukeroku sushi), all of which originated as the teahouse in front of our hospital. <ref name=":0" /> operates within the hospital grounds and nearby areas. Similar products can also be found in surrounding areas, such as {{ill|lt=Roadside Station Menuma|Q11640968|WD=Q11640968}}'s ``{{ill|lt=Ginko Ogino|Q4794092|WD=Q4794092|lt=Gingin}} Sushi.''On {{ill|lt=Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|Q1376786|WD=Q1376786}}'s "My Local Cuisine" website, it is introduced under the name "Shoten Sushi", which originates from our hospital.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shoten Sushi Saitama Prefecture {{!}} Our local cuisine: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|url=https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/33_29_saitama.html|website=www.maff.go.jp|access-date=2026-01-17}}</ref> etc.<ref group="Note">It is also sometimes written as "Shoten Sushi". It is presumed that all of these names are misspelled from the shop name <!-- Shoten Sushi --> of the three shops mentioned above, which faces the temple grounds, and it seems inappropriate as a unified name for the three shops. </ref>In the past, there was no unified name, but as a tourist guide for Kumagaya City, it was advertised under the name ``''Menuma no Inarizushi''. Kumagaya City Tourism Association Official Homepage|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, as this name has also been applied and registered in the 100-year food program mentioned below, in recent years, each of the 4 “Nagai Inari Sushi from the Menuma area” products, including Gingin Sushi, have been introduced.<ref name=":0" It is common to refer to the general term ``'''Menuma no Inarizushi''''.March 3, 2023, {{ill|lt=Agency for Cultural Affairs|Q1009519|WD=Q1009519}} “{{ill|lt=100 Years of Food|Q134383966|WD=Q134383966}}” “100 Years of Traditional Food Category ～Local cuisine that has continued since the Edo period～” <ref>[https://foodculture2021.go.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/r4_100nenfood.pdf List of “100 Year Food” by prefecture (FY2020)]</ref>.

[[File:Kisoumon.jpg|thumb|240px|Kisoumon]]'''Kangiin'' is {{ill|lt=Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|WD=Q128186}}{{ill|lt=Kumagaya City|Q41106|WD=Q41106}}{{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684| It is {{ill|lt=Buddhism|Q748|WD=Q748}}{{ill|lt=temple|Q5393308|WD=Q5393308}} of {{ill|lt=Koyasan Shingon sect|Q3077357|WD=Q3077357}} located in Menuma}}. {{ill|lt=Kankiten#Japan's three great holy deities|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315|lt=Japan's three great holy deities}} It is generally referred to as ``Menuma Shodenzan,'' which is a place name attached to the mountain name, and is mainly used in official guides.
Also, "Saitama {{ill|lt=Nikko Toshogu|Q696641|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikko}}" (before it was designated as a national treasure, it was "Saitama's Konikko") |publisher= local publisher |isbn= 4-87663-703-2 |date= 2004-09}}</ref> ). It is called ``Shoten-sama (of Menuma)'' by worshipers and local residents.

=== History ===
According to temple legend, in the 3rd year of Jisho ({{ill|lt=1179|Q19698|WD=Q19698}}), the military commander {{ill|lt=Sanemori Saito|Q3472140|WD=Q3472140|lt=It is said that Fujibetsuto Sanemori}} built Shotengu Shrine to enshrine the guardian deity Daisei {{ill|lt=Kankiten|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315}} (Shoten) and made it the general guardian of Nagaisho. Later, in the 8th year of Kenkyu (1197), Ryo'o Sozu (Sanenaga, the second son of Saito Betto Sanemori) built Kangi-in Choraku-ji Temple as the Betto temple (honbo) of Shotengu Shrine, and it is said that {{ill|lt=Eleven-faced Kannon|Q11404731|WD=Q11404731}} was the principal image.

{{ill|lt=Kamakura Shogunate|Q736839|WD=Q736839}}'s first shogun, {{ill|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|WD=Q242800}}, visited the shrine, and in the medieval period it was protected by the lord of Oshi Castle, and in the early modern period it was rebuilt by {{ill|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|WD=Q171977}}, but it was destroyed by the Great Menuma Fire in 1670. The current Shotendo (main shrine) was rebuilt between the Kyoho and Horeki eras (mid-18th century).

Restoration work on the main shrine was carried out from 2003 to 2011, and the completion ceremony for the main building was held on January 18, 2010, and the completion ceremony was held on June 1, 2011, and it opened to the public on the same day. On July 9, 2012, Seitendo (main shrine) was designated as a {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795}} (the first designation as a National Treasure building in Saitama Prefecture).

=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
; Seitendo (main hall)
: It is a mausoleum-style {{ill|lt=Gongen-zukuri|Q3155268|WD=Q3155268}} building (an architectural style that combines multiple buildings, as seen in Nikko Toshogu Shrine, etc.), which consists of a worship hall, a middle hall (so-ma), and a back hall. The master carpenter was the master carpenter Hayashi Hyogo Masakiyo of Menuma, a descendant of {{ill|lt=Masanobu Hiranai|Q11482097|WD=Q11482097}}, the master carpenter of the shogunate.The building was rebuilt over a period of more than 20 years, from 1735 to 1760, by his son Masanobu. The inner hall is a gambrel-style structure with 3 girders and 3 girders, with a front facing prayer hall.The middle hall is Ryosage-zukuri, with 3 girder rows and 1 girder.The worship hall is gambrel-style, with 5 girder rows and 3 beams.These are connected to form a single building, and the roof is all roofed with tile-rod copper plates.: The inner and outer halls are highly decorative with splendid carvings, lacquering, coloring, metal fittings, etc. both inside and outside. The ``eagle and monkey'' carvings on the paneling on the south side of the inner hall are said to have been created by the legendary carving craftsman {{ill|lt=Hidashi Jingoro|Q2668220|WD=Q2668220}}, but the actual master carvers were Ginpachiro Ishihara (Ginpachi) and Bunjiro Sekiguchi. In the inner hall, the pillars, pushpieces, and other members are carved with ground patterns, and the large paneling under the inner law is decorated with the Seven Lucky Gods, and the area under the rim is decorated with colored carvings depicting the theme of playing with karako. Each of the carvings has a theme related to a Chinese story, such as ``Three Saints' Susan'' and ``{{ill|lt=Sima Guang|Q33566|WD=Q33566|lt=Sima Wengong}}'s Bottle Breaker'' under the kara gable, and ``Kotogi Calligraphy'' under the kara gable in front of the shrine. Repairs were carried out from 2003 to 2010, mainly re-roofing and coloring, and the original coloring was restored. Designated as {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795}} in 2012<ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.bunka.go.jp/ima/press_release/pdf/jubunkenzou_shittei_240521.pdf About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) (Agency for Cultural Affairs)]}}</ref>{{deadurl|date=July 2018}}<ref>Designation of National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties (Buildings) in 2012 ○From National Treasures (Buildings){{Cite book|Japanese book|title= White Paper on Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Chapter 8 Part 2 / Trends and developments in education, science and technology policies - Realizing a nation built on culture and the arts |chapter=Designated on July 9, 2012 (1 item in total) Kangi-in Seitendo |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/hakusho/html/hpab201301/1338525_019.pdf|format = PDF |page= 294|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2018-07-10}}</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 106 of July 9, 2012</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url= http://www.city.kumagaya.lg.jp/kanko/midokoro/menumasyoudenzan/kangiinkokuho.html |title=“Kangi-in Seitendo” designated as a national treasure|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2012-07-12|publisher= Kumagaya City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|Japanese book|others= Cultural Properties Protection Committee; Agency for Cultural Affairs Cultural Properties Protection Department |title = Newly designated cultural properties |work= Monthly cultural properties |publisher = Daiichi Hoki Publishing |number= 586|year = 2012|issn= 0016-5948 |ncid= AN00221652}}</ref>.
