=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
; Seitendo (main hall)
: It is a mausoleum-style {{ill|lt=Gongen-zukuri|Q3155268|WD=Q3155268|1=Ishi-no-ma-zukuri}} building (an architectural style that combines multiple buildings, as seen in Nikko Toshogu Shrine, etc.), which consists of a worship hall, a middle hall (so-ma), and a back hall. The master carpenter was the master carpenter Hayashi Hyogo Masakiyo of Menuma, a descendant of {{ill|lt=Masanobu Hiranai|Q11482097|WD=Q11482097|1=Heinouchi Masanobu}}, the master carpenter of the shogunate.The building was rebuilt over a period of more than 20 years, from 1735 to 1760, by his son Masanobu. The inner hall is a gambrel-style structure with 3 girders and 3 girders, with a front facing prayer hall.The middle hall is Ryosage-zukuri, with 3 girder rows and 1 girder.The worship hall is gambrel-style, with 5 girder rows and 3 beams.These are connected to form a single building, and the roof is all roofed with tile-rod copper plates.: The inner and outer halls are highly decorative with splendid carvings, lacquering, coloring, metal fittings, etc. both inside and outside. The ``eagle and monkey'' carvings on the paneling on the south side of the inner hall are said to have been created by the legendary carving craftsman {{ill|lt=Hidashi Jingoro|Q2668220|WD=Q2668220|1=Hidari Jingorō}}, but the actual master carvers were Ginpachiro Ishihara (Ginpachi) and Bunjiro Sekiguchi. In the inner hall, the pillars, pushpieces, and other members are carved with ground patterns, and the large paneling under the inner law is decorated with the Seven Lucky Gods, and the area under the rim is decorated with colored carvings depicting the theme of playing with karako. Each of the carvings has a theme related to a Chinese story, such as ``Three Saints' Susan'' and ``{{ill|lt=Sima Guang|Q33566|WD=Q33566|lt=Sima Wengong|1=Sima Guang}}'s Bottle Breaker'' under the kara gable, and ``Kotogi Calligraphy'' under the kara gable in front of the shrine. Repairs were carried out from 2003 to 2010, mainly re-roofing and coloring, and the original coloring was restored. Designated as {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} in 2012<ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.bunka.go.jp/ima/press_release/pdf/jubunkenzou_shittei_240521.pdf About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) (Agency for Cultural Affairs)]}}</ref>{{deadurl|date=July 2018}}<ref>Designation of National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties (Buildings) in 2012 ○From National Treasures (Buildings){{Cite book|Japanese book|title= White Paper on Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Chapter 8 Part 2 / Trends and developments in education, science and technology policies - Realizing a nation built on culture and the arts |chapter=Designated on July 9, 2012 (1 item in total) Kangi-in Seitendo |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/hakusho/html/hpab201301/1338525_019.pdf|format = PDF |page= 294|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2018-07-10}}</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 106 of July 9, 2012</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url= http://www.city.kumagaya.lg.jp/kanko/midokoro/menumasyoudenzan/kangiinkokuho.html |title=“Kangi-in Seitendo” designated as a national treasure|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2012-07-12|publisher= Kumagaya City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|Japanese book|others= Cultural Properties Protection Committee; Agency for Cultural Affairs Cultural Properties Protection Department |title = Newly designated cultural properties |work= Monthly cultural properties |publisher = Daiichi Hoki Publishing |number= 586|year = 2012|issn= 0016-5948 |ncid= AN00221652}}</ref>.

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
[[File:Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|The statues of Kangiten and Two Doji are cast in the center. ]]
*Kisomon - An 18m high copper plate roofed eight-legged gate located at the front entrance of the temple grounds. This unique gate has a double roof, upper and lower, with two gable roofs at the front and back, and when viewed from the side, has three gables. Statues of Jikokuten and Tamonten are placed on the left and right. It was built by Masamichi Hayashi of Menuma in the 4th year of the Kaei era, and completed around 1855.
*Shakujoto - The secret principal image of Buddha in Shotendo. There is an inscription dating back to 1197, and the statues of Kangiten and Nidoji are cast in the center. A shakujo is a staff held by Jizo Bodhisattva and others, and the head of the staff sometimes represents a Buddha statue.

=== Inarizushi in Menuma ===
[[File:Menuma Inari-zushi 01.JPG|thumb|200px|Menuma Inari-zushi]]
It has been eaten since the Edo period, mainly by visitors to our hospital. Kumagaya City Tourism Association official website|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, {{ill|lt=Inari sushi|Q874397|WD=Q874397|1=Inarizushi}} is a specialty of the Menuma district (formerly {{ill|lt=Menuma Town|Q6817684|WD=Q6817684|1=Menuma, Saitama}}). It is characterized by its elongated shape, which is different from typical Inari sushi.Before the war, on the contrary, this elongated shape was common, but after the war, with the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=contract processing system|1=UNKNOWN}}, the standard was reduced to the size of nigiri sushi. However, in the Menuma area, efforts were made to maintain the elongated shape, resulting in the sushi being a specialty that continues to this day. To be a "jumbo"...Submit a report and keep the size Kumagaya's Jumbo Inari "100 Year Food" certification report meeting (Saitama Shimbun) - Yahoo! News]</ref>. In recent years, it has become popular as a specialty attached to the national treasure (main shrine).

{{ill|lt=Maki sushi|Q5739461|WD=Q5739461|1=Makizushi}} Three sushi restaurants specialize in this set (Sukeroku sushi), all of which originated as the teahouse in front of our hospital. <ref name=":0" /> operates within the hospital grounds and nearby areas. Similar products can also be found in surrounding areas, such as {{ill|lt=Roadside Station Menuma|Q11640968|WD=Q11640968|1=Roadside station Menuma}}'s ``{{ill|lt=Ginko Ogino|Q4794092|WD=Q4794092|lt=Gingin|1=Ogino Ginko}} Sushi.''On {{ill|lt=Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|Q1376786|WD=Q1376786|1=Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (Japan)}}'s "My Local Cuisine" website, it is introduced under the name "Shoten Sushi", which originates from our hospital.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shoten Sushi Saitama Prefecture {{!}} Our local cuisine: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|url=https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/33_29_saitama.html|website=www.maff.go.jp|access-date=2026-01-17}}</ref> etc.<ref group="Note">It is also sometimes written as "Shoten Sushi". It is presumed that all of these names are misspelled from the shop name <!-- Shoten Sushi --> of the three shops mentioned above, which faces the temple grounds, and it seems inappropriate as a unified name for the three shops. </ref>In the past, there was no unified name, but as a tourist guide for Kumagaya City, it was advertised under the name ``''Menuma no Inarizushi''. Kumagaya City Tourism Association Official Homepage|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, as this name has also been applied and registered in the 100-year food program mentioned below, in recent years, each of the 4 “Nagai Inari Sushi from the Menuma area” products, including Gingin Sushi, have been introduced.<ref name=":0" It is common to refer to the general term ``'''Menuma no Inarizushi''''.March 3, 2023, {{ill|lt=Agency for Cultural Affairs|Q1009519|WD=Q1009519|1=Agency for Cultural Affairs}} “{{ill|lt=100 Years of Food|Q134383966|WD=Q134383966|1=100 Years of Food}}” “100 Years of Traditional Food Category ～Local cuisine that has continued since the Edo period～” <ref>[https://foodculture2021.go.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/r4_100nenfood.pdf List of “100 Year Food” by prefecture (FY2020)]</ref>.

*: Since the shrine is crowded during New Year's holidays and during spring and autumn festivals, Kumagaya City recommends parking at the Menuma Tourist Parking Lot in the south and taking a stroll around the shrine.

[[File:Kisoumon.jpg|thumb|240px|Kisoumon]]'''Kangiin'' is {{ill|lt=Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|WD=Q128186|1=Saitama Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Kumagaya City|Q41106|WD=Q41106|1=Kumagaya}}{{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684| It is {{ill|lt=Buddhism|Q748|WD=Q748|1=Buddhism}}{{ill|lt=temple|Q5393308|WD=Q5393308|1=Buddhist temple}} of {{ill|lt=Koyasan Shingon sect|Q3077357|WD=Q3077357|1=Kōyasan Shingon-shū}} located in Menuma}}. {{ill|lt=Kankiten#Japan's three great holy deities|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315|lt=Japan's three great holy deities|1=Kangiten}} It is generally referred to as ``Menuma Shodenzan,'' which is a place name attached to the mountain name, and is mainly used in official guides.
Also, "Saitama {{ill|lt=Nikko Toshogu|Q696641|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikko|1=Nikkō Tōshō-gū}}" (before it was designated as a national treasure, it was "Saitama's Konikko") |publisher= local publisher |isbn= 4-87663-703-2 |date= 2004-09}}</ref> ). It is called ``Shoten-sama (of Menuma)'' by worshipers and local residents.

=== History ===
According to temple legend, in the 3rd year of Jisho ({{ill|lt=1179|Q19698|WD=Q19698|1=1179}}), the military commander {{ill|lt=Sanemori Saito|Q3472140|WD=Q3472140|lt=It is said that Fujibetsuto Sanemori|1=Sanemori Saitō}} built Shotengu Shrine to enshrine the guardian deity Daisei {{ill|lt=Kankiten|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315|1=Kangiten}} (Shoten) and made it the general guardian of Nagaisho. Later, in the 8th year of Kenkyu (1197), Ryo'o Sozu (Sanenaga, the second son of Saito Betto Sanemori) built Kangi-in Choraku-ji Temple as the Betto temple (honbo) of Shotengu Shrine, and it is said that {{ill|lt=Eleven-faced Kannon|Q11404731|WD=Q11404731|1=Ekādaśamukha}} was the principal image.

{{ill|lt=Kamakura Shogunate|Q736839|WD=Q736839|1=Kamakura shogunate}}'s first shogun, {{ill|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|WD=Q242800|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, visited the shrine, and in the medieval period it was protected by the lord of Oshi Castle, and in the early modern period it was rebuilt by {{ill|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|WD=Q171977|1=Tokugawa Ieyasu}}, but it was destroyed by the Great Menuma Fire in 1670. The current Shotendo (main shrine) was rebuilt between the Kyoho and Horeki eras (mid-18th century).

Restoration work on the main shrine was carried out from 2003 to 2011, and the completion ceremony for the main building was held on January 18, 2010, and the completion ceremony was held on June 1, 2011, and it opened to the public on the same day. On July 9, 2012, Seitendo (main shrine) was designated as a {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} (the first designation as a National Treasure building in Saitama Prefecture).

=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
; Seitendo (main hall)
: It is a mausoleum-style {{ill|lt=Gongen-zukuri|Q3155268|WD=Q3155268|1=Ishi-no-ma-zukuri}} building (an architectural style that combines multiple buildings, as seen in Nikko Toshogu Shrine, etc.), which consists of a worship hall, a middle hall (so-ma), and a back hall. The master carpenter was the master carpenter Hayashi Hyogo Masakiyo of Menuma, a descendant of {{ill|lt=Masanobu Hiranai|Q11482097|WD=Q11482097|1=Heinouchi Masanobu}}, the master carpenter of the shogunate.The building was rebuilt over a period of more than 20 years, from 1735 to 1760, by his son Masanobu. The inner hall is a gambrel-style structure with 3 girders and 3 girders, with a front facing prayer hall.The middle hall is Ryosage-zukuri, with 3 girder rows and 1 girder.The worship hall is gambrel-style, with 5 girder rows and 3 beams.These are connected to form a single building, and the roof is all roofed with tile-rod copper plates.: The inner and outer halls are highly decorative with splendid carvings, lacquering, coloring, metal fittings, etc. both inside and outside. The ``eagle and monkey'' carvings on the paneling on the south side of the inner hall are said to have been created by the legendary carving craftsman {{ill|lt=Hidashi Jingoro|Q2668220|WD=Q2668220|1=Hidari Jingorō}}, but the actual master carvers were Ginpachiro Ishihara (Ginpachi) and Bunjiro Sekiguchi. In the inner hall, the pillars, pushpieces, and other members are carved with ground patterns, and the large paneling under the inner law is decorated with the Seven Lucky Gods, and the area under the rim is decorated with colored carvings depicting the theme of playing with karako. Each of the carvings has a theme related to a Chinese story, such as ``Three Saints' Susan'' and ``{{ill|lt=Sima Guang|Q33566|WD=Q33566|lt=Sima Wengong|1=Sima Guang}}'s Bottle Breaker'' under the kara gable, and ``Kotogi Calligraphy'' under the kara gable in front of the shrine. Repairs were carried out from 2003 to 2010, mainly re-roofing and coloring, and the original coloring was restored. Designated as {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} in 2012<ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.bunka.go.jp/ima/press_release/pdf/jubunkenzou_shittei_240521.pdf About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) (Agency for Cultural Affairs)]}}</ref>{{deadurl|date=July 2018}}<ref>Designation of National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties (Buildings) in 2012 ○From National Treasures (Buildings){{Cite book|Japanese book|title= White Paper on Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Chapter 8 Part 2 / Trends and developments in education, science and technology policies - Realizing a nation built on culture and the arts |chapter=Designated on July 9, 2012 (1 item in total) Kangi-in Seitendo |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/hakusho/html/hpab201301/1338525_019.pdf|format = PDF |page= 294|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2018-07-10}}</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 106 of July 9, 2012</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url= http://www.city.kumagaya.lg.jp/kanko/midokoro/menumasyoudenzan/kangiinkokuho.html |title=“Kangi-in Seitendo” designated as a national treasure|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2012-07-12|publisher= Kumagaya City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|Japanese book|others= Cultural Properties Protection Committee; Agency for Cultural Affairs Cultural Properties Protection Department |title = Newly designated cultural properties |work= Monthly cultural properties |publisher = Daiichi Hoki Publishing |number= 586|year = 2012|issn= 0016-5948 |ncid= AN00221652}}</ref>.

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
[[File:Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|The statues of Kangiten and Two Doji are cast in the center. ]]
*Kisomon - An 18m high copper plate roofed eight-legged gate located at the front entrance of the temple grounds. This unique gate has a double roof, upper and lower, with two gable roofs at the front and back, and when viewed from the side, has three gables. Statues of Jikokuten and Tamonten are placed on the left and right. It was built by Masamichi Hayashi of Menuma in the 4th year of the Kaei era, and completed around 1855.
*Shakujoto - The secret principal image of Buddha in Shotendo. There is an inscription dating back to 1197, and the statues of Kangiten and Nidoji are cast in the center. A shakujo is a staff held by Jizo Bodhisattva and others, and the head of the staff sometimes represents a Buddha statue.

=== Inarizushi in Menuma ===
[[File:Menuma Inari-zushi 01.JPG|thumb|200px|Menuma Inari-zushi]]
It has been eaten since the Edo period, mainly by visitors to our hospital. Kumagaya City Tourism Association official website|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, {{ill|lt=Inari sushi|Q874397|WD=Q874397|1=Inarizushi}} is a specialty of the Menuma district (formerly {{ill|lt=Menuma Town|Q6817684|WD=Q6817684|1=Menuma, Saitama}}). It is characterized by its elongated shape, which is different from typical Inari sushi.Before the war, on the contrary, this elongated shape was common, but after the war, with the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=contract processing system|1=UNKNOWN}}, the standard was reduced to the size of nigiri sushi. However, in the Menuma area, efforts were made to maintain the elongated shape, resulting in the sushi being a specialty that continues to this day. To be a "jumbo"...Submit a report and keep the size Kumagaya's Jumbo Inari "100 Year Food" certification report meeting (Saitama Shimbun) - Yahoo! News]</ref>. In recent years, it has become popular as a specialty attached to the national treasure (main shrine).

{{ill|lt=Maki sushi|Q5739461|WD=Q5739461|1=Makizushi}} Three sushi restaurants specialize in this set (Sukeroku sushi), all of which originated as the teahouse in front of our hospital. <ref name=":0" /> operates within the hospital grounds and nearby areas. Similar products can also be found in surrounding areas, such as {{ill|lt=Roadside Station Menuma|Q11640968|WD=Q11640968|1=Roadside station Menuma}}'s ``{{ill|lt=Ginko Ogino|Q4794092|WD=Q4794092|lt=Gingin|1=Ogino Ginko}} Sushi.''On {{ill|lt=Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|Q1376786|WD=Q1376786|1=Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (Japan)}}'s "My Local Cuisine" website, it is introduced under the name "Shoten Sushi", which originates from our hospital.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shoten Sushi Saitama Prefecture {{!}} Our local cuisine: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|url=https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/33_29_saitama.html|website=www.maff.go.jp|access-date=2026-01-17}}</ref> etc.<ref group="Note">It is also sometimes written as "Shoten Sushi". It is presumed that all of these names are misspelled from the shop name <!-- Shoten Sushi --> of the three shops mentioned above, which faces the temple grounds, and it seems inappropriate as a unified name for the three shops. </ref>In the past, there was no unified name, but as a tourist guide for Kumagaya City, it was advertised under the name ``''Menuma no Inarizushi''. Kumagaya City Tourism Association Official Homepage|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, as this name has also been applied and registered in the 100-year food program mentioned below, in recent years, each of the 4 “Nagai Inari Sushi from the Menuma area” products, including Gingin Sushi, have been introduced.<ref name=":0" It is common to refer to the general term ``'''Menuma no Inarizushi''''.March 3, 2023, {{ill|lt=Agency for Cultural Affairs|Q1009519|WD=Q1009519|1=Agency for Cultural Affairs}} “{{ill|lt=100 Years of Food|Q134383966|WD=Q134383966|1=100 Years of Food}}” “100 Years of Traditional Food Category ～Local cuisine that has continued since the Edo period～” <ref>[https://foodculture2021.go.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/r4_100nenfood.pdf List of “100 Year Food” by prefecture (FY2020)]</ref>.

=== Transportation ===

=== car ===
*{{ill|lt=Gunma Prefectural Road/Saitama Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line|Q11609884|WD=Q11609884|lt=Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line|1=Gunma Prefectural Road and Saitama Prefectural Road Route 341}} Along. In addition, between the main hall and the main temple, {{ill|lt=Saitama Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumuma Line|Q11427072|WD=Q11427072|lt=Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumanum Line|1=Saitama Prefectural Road Route 59}} runs, and is called ``Enmusubi Dori'' (because this hospital is said to have {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=divine blessings|1=UNKNOWN}} for matchmaking).
*: There is a private parking lot nearby. However, the parking spaces facing the approach between the Ota Kumagaya Line and Kisomon Gate and the 6th parking lot behind the main shrine are not available for use by worshipers (please refer to the official website and local information).
*: Since the shrine is crowded during New Year's holidays and during spring and autumn festivals, Kumagaya City recommends parking at the Menuma Tourist Parking Lot in the south and taking a stroll around the shrine.

=== Bus ===
*{{ill|lt=Asahi Motors|Q11517584|WD=Q11517584|lt=Asahi Bus|1=Asahi Motor}}: {{ill|lt=Kumagaya Station|Q735594|WD=Q735594|1=Kumagaya Station}} North Exit Platform 6 - [KM61] {{ill|lt=Ota Station (Gunma Prefecture)|Q8081729|WD=Q8081729|lt=Ota Station|1=Ōta Station (Gunma)}} line/[KM63] Take the bus bound for {{ill|lt=Nishikoizumi Station|Q11627702|WD=Q11627702|1=Nishi-Koizumi Station}}/[KM64] Menuma Shotenmae<ref group="Notes">[KM65] Menuma, get off at the "Menuma Shimomachi" stop, and walk for 13 minutes. </ref>, get off at the "Menuma Shoten-mae" stop. *Late-night hours after 10pm depart from bus stop 3 (destinations above + [KM62] bound for Nishiyajima are also available)
*{{ill|lt=Yu-Yu Bus (Kumagaya City)|Q11280693|WD=Q11280693|lt=Yu-Yu Bus|1=Kumagaya City Community Bus}} (Community Bus): Glider (Kumagaya Station South Exit - Menuma Administrative Center), Glider Wagon (Menuma Circulation), get off at the "Menuma Shoten-mae" stop or the "Shotenzan Minami Entrance" stop.

[[File:Saito Sanemori Statue Menuma 01.jpg|thumb|240px|Saito Sanemori Statue]]
[[File:Kisoumon.jpg|thumb|240px|Kisoumon]]'''Kangiin'' is {{ill|lt=Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|WD=Q128186|1=Saitama Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Kumagaya City|Q41106|WD=Q41106|1=Kumagaya}}{{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684| It is {{ill|lt=Buddhism|Q748|WD=Q748|1=Buddhism}}{{ill|lt=temple|Q5393308|WD=Q5393308|1=Buddhist temple}} of {{ill|lt=Koyasan Shingon sect|Q3077357|WD=Q3077357|1=Kōyasan Shingon-shū}} located in Menuma}}. {{ill|lt=Kankiten#Japan's three great holy deities|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315|lt=Japan's three great holy deities|1=Kangiten}} It is generally referred to as ``Menuma Shodenzan,'' which is a place name attached to the mountain name, and is mainly used in official guides.
Also, "Saitama {{ill|lt=Nikko Toshogu|Q696641|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikko|1=Nikkō Tōshō-gū}}" (before it was designated as a national treasure, it was "Saitama's Konikko") |publisher= local publisher |isbn= 4-87663-703-2 |date= 2004-09}}</ref> ). It is called ``Shoten-sama (of Menuma)'' by worshipers and local residents.

=== History ===
According to temple legend, in the 3rd year of Jisho ({{ill|lt=1179|Q19698|WD=Q19698|1=1179}}), the military commander {{ill|lt=Sanemori Saito|Q3472140|WD=Q3472140|lt=It is said that Fujibetsuto Sanemori|1=Sanemori Saitō}} built Shotengu Shrine to enshrine the guardian deity Daisei {{ill|lt=Kankiten|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315|1=Kangiten}} (Shoten) and made it the general guardian of Nagaisho. Later, in the 8th year of Kenkyu (1197), Ryo'o Sozu (Sanenaga, the second son of Saito Betto Sanemori) built Kangi-in Choraku-ji Temple as the Betto temple (honbo) of Shotengu Shrine, and it is said that {{ill|lt=Eleven-faced Kannon|Q11404731|WD=Q11404731|1=Ekādaśamukha}} was the principal image.

{{ill|lt=Kamakura Shogunate|Q736839|WD=Q736839|1=Kamakura shogunate}}'s first shogun, {{ill|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|WD=Q242800|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, visited the shrine, and in the medieval period it was protected by the lord of Oshi Castle, and in the early modern period it was rebuilt by {{ill|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|WD=Q171977|1=Tokugawa Ieyasu}}, but it was destroyed by the Great Menuma Fire in 1670. The current Shotendo (main shrine) was rebuilt between the Kyoho and Horeki eras (mid-18th century).

Restoration work on the main shrine was carried out from 2003 to 2011, and the completion ceremony for the main building was held on January 18, 2010, and the completion ceremony was held on June 1, 2011, and it opened to the public on the same day. On July 9, 2012, Seitendo (main shrine) was designated as a {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} (the first designation as a National Treasure building in Saitama Prefecture).

=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
; Seitendo (main hall)
: It is a mausoleum-style {{ill|lt=Gongen-zukuri|Q3155268|WD=Q3155268|1=Ishi-no-ma-zukuri}} building (an architectural style that combines multiple buildings, as seen in Nikko Toshogu Shrine, etc.), which consists of a worship hall, a middle hall (so-ma), and a back hall. The master carpenter was the master carpenter Hayashi Hyogo Masakiyo of Menuma, a descendant of {{ill|lt=Masanobu Hiranai|Q11482097|WD=Q11482097|1=Heinouchi Masanobu}}, the master carpenter of the shogunate.The building was rebuilt over a period of more than 20 years, from 1735 to 1760, by his son Masanobu. The inner hall is a gambrel-style structure with 3 girders and 3 girders, with a front facing prayer hall.The middle hall is Ryosage-zukuri, with 3 girder rows and 1 girder.The worship hall is gambrel-style, with 5 girder rows and 3 beams.These are connected to form a single building, and the roof is all roofed with tile-rod copper plates.: The inner and outer halls are highly decorative with splendid carvings, lacquering, coloring, metal fittings, etc. both inside and outside. The ``eagle and monkey'' carvings on the paneling on the south side of the inner hall are said to have been created by the legendary carving craftsman {{ill|lt=Hidashi Jingoro|Q2668220|WD=Q2668220|1=Hidari Jingorō}}, but the actual master carvers were Ginpachiro Ishihara (Ginpachi) and Bunjiro Sekiguchi. In the inner hall, the pillars, pushpieces, and other members are carved with ground patterns, and the large paneling under the inner law is decorated with the Seven Lucky Gods, and the area under the rim is decorated with colored carvings depicting the theme of playing with karako. Each of the carvings has a theme related to a Chinese story, such as ``Three Saints' Susan'' and ``{{ill|lt=Sima Guang|Q33566|WD=Q33566|lt=Sima Wengong|1=Sima Guang}}'s Bottle Breaker'' under the kara gable, and ``Kotogi Calligraphy'' under the kara gable in front of the shrine. Repairs were carried out from 2003 to 2010, mainly re-roofing and coloring, and the original coloring was restored. Designated as {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} in 2012<ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.bunka.go.jp/ima/press_release/pdf/jubunkenzou_shittei_240521.pdf About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) (Agency for Cultural Affairs)]}}</ref>{{deadurl|date=July 2018}}<ref>Designation of National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties (Buildings) in 2012 ○From National Treasures (Buildings){{Cite book|Japanese book|title= White Paper on Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Chapter 8 Part 2 / Trends and developments in education, science and technology policies - Realizing a nation built on culture and the arts |chapter=Designated on July 9, 2012 (1 item in total) Kangi-in Seitendo |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/hakusho/html/hpab201301/1338525_019.pdf|format = PDF |page= 294|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2018-07-10}}</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 106 of July 9, 2012</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url= http://www.city.kumagaya.lg.jp/kanko/midokoro/menumasyoudenzan/kangiinkokuho.html |title=“Kangi-in Seitendo” designated as a national treasure|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2012-07-12|publisher= Kumagaya City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|Japanese book|others= Cultural Properties Protection Committee; Agency for Cultural Affairs Cultural Properties Protection Department |title = Newly designated cultural properties |work= Monthly cultural properties |publisher = Daiichi Hoki Publishing |number= 586|year = 2012|issn= 0016-5948 |ncid= AN00221652}}</ref>.

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
[[File:Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|The statues of Kangiten and Two Doji are cast in the center. ]]
*Kisomon - An 18m high copper plate roofed eight-legged gate located at the front entrance of the temple grounds. This unique gate has a double roof, upper and lower, with two gable roofs at the front and back, and when viewed from the side, has three gables. Statues of Jikokuten and Tamonten are placed on the left and right. It was built by Masamichi Hayashi of Menuma in the 4th year of the Kaei era, and completed around 1855.
*Shakujoto - The secret principal image of Buddha in Shotendo. There is an inscription dating back to 1197, and the statues of Kangiten and Nidoji are cast in the center. A shakujo is a staff held by Jizo Bodhisattva and others, and the head of the staff sometimes represents a Buddha statue.

=== Inarizushi in Menuma ===
[[File:Menuma Inari-zushi 01.JPG|thumb|200px|Menuma Inari-zushi]]
It has been eaten since the Edo period, mainly by visitors to our hospital. Kumagaya City Tourism Association official website|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, {{ill|lt=Inari sushi|Q874397|WD=Q874397|1=Inarizushi}} is a specialty of the Menuma district (formerly {{ill|lt=Menuma Town|Q6817684|WD=Q6817684|1=Menuma, Saitama}}). It is characterized by its elongated shape, which is different from typical Inari sushi.Before the war, on the contrary, this elongated shape was common, but after the war, with the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=contract processing system|1=UNKNOWN}}, the standard was reduced to the size of nigiri sushi. However, in the Menuma area, efforts were made to maintain the elongated shape, resulting in the sushi being a specialty that continues to this day. To be a "jumbo"...Submit a report and keep the size Kumagaya's Jumbo Inari "100 Year Food" certification report meeting (Saitama Shimbun) - Yahoo! News]</ref>. In recent years, it has become popular as a specialty attached to the national treasure (main shrine).

{{ill|lt=Maki sushi|Q5739461|WD=Q5739461|1=Makizushi}} Three sushi restaurants specialize in this set (Sukeroku sushi), all of which originated as the teahouse in front of our hospital. <ref name=":0" /> operates within the hospital grounds and nearby areas. Similar products can also be found in surrounding areas, such as {{ill|lt=Roadside Station Menuma|Q11640968|WD=Q11640968|1=Roadside station Menuma}}'s ``{{ill|lt=Ginko Ogino|Q4794092|WD=Q4794092|lt=Gingin|1=Ogino Ginko}} Sushi.''On {{ill|lt=Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|Q1376786|WD=Q1376786|1=Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (Japan)}}'s "My Local Cuisine" website, it is introduced under the name "Shoten Sushi", which originates from our hospital.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shoten Sushi Saitama Prefecture {{!}} Our local cuisine: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|url=https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/33_29_saitama.html|website=www.maff.go.jp|access-date=2026-01-17}}</ref> etc.<ref group="Note">It is also sometimes written as "Shoten Sushi". It is presumed that all of these names are misspelled from the shop name <!-- Shoten Sushi --> of the three shops mentioned above, which faces the temple grounds, and it seems inappropriate as a unified name for the three shops. </ref>In the past, there was no unified name, but as a tourist guide for Kumagaya City, it was advertised under the name ``''Menuma no Inarizushi''. Kumagaya City Tourism Association Official Homepage|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, as this name has also been applied and registered in the 100-year food program mentioned below, in recent years, each of the 4 “Nagai Inari Sushi from the Menuma area” products, including Gingin Sushi, have been introduced.<ref name=":0" It is common to refer to the general term ``'''Menuma no Inarizushi''''.March 3, 2023, {{ill|lt=Agency for Cultural Affairs|Q1009519|WD=Q1009519|1=Agency for Cultural Affairs}} “{{ill|lt=100 Years of Food|Q134383966|WD=Q134383966|1=100 Years of Food}}” “100 Years of Traditional Food Category ～Local cuisine that has continued since the Edo period～” <ref>[https://foodculture2021.go.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/r4_100nenfood.pdf List of “100 Year Food” by prefecture (FY2020)]</ref>.

=== car ===
*{{ill|lt=Gunma Prefectural Road/Saitama Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line|Q11609884|WD=Q11609884|lt=Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line|1=Gunma Prefectural Road and Saitama Prefectural Road Route 341}} Along. In addition, between the main hall and the main temple, {{ill|lt=Saitama Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumuma Line|Q11427072|WD=Q11427072|lt=Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumanum Line|1=Saitama Prefectural Road Route 59}} runs, and is called ``Enmusubi Dori'' (because this hospital is said to have {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=divine blessings|1=UNKNOWN}} for matchmaking).
*: There is a private parking lot nearby. However, the parking spaces facing the approach between the Ota Kumagaya Line and Kisomon Gate and the 6th parking lot behind the main shrine are not available for use by worshipers (please refer to the official website and local information).
*: Since the shrine is crowded during New Year's holidays and during spring and autumn festivals, Kumagaya City recommends parking at the Menuma Tourist Parking Lot in the south and taking a stroll around the shrine.

[[File:Kisoumon.jpg|thumb|240px|Kisoumon]]'''Kangiin'' is {{ill|lt=Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|WD=Q128186|1=Saitama Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Kumagaya City|Q41106|WD=Q41106|1=Kumagaya}}{{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684| It is {{ill|lt=Buddhism|Q748|WD=Q748|1=Buddhism}}{{ill|lt=temple|Q5393308|WD=Q5393308|1=Buddhist temple}} of {{ill|lt=Koyasan Shingon sect|Q3077357|WD=Q3077357|1=Kōyasan Shingon-shū}} located in Menuma}}. {{ill|lt=Kankiten#Japan's three great holy deities|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315|lt=Japan's three great holy deities|1=Kangiten}} It is generally referred to as ``Menuma Shodenzan,'' which is a place name attached to the mountain name, and is mainly used in official guides.
Also, "Saitama {{ill|lt=Nikko Toshogu|Q696641|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikko|1=Nikkō Tōshō-gū}}" (before it was designated as a national treasure, it was "Saitama's Konikko") |publisher= local publisher |isbn= 4-87663-703-2 |date= 2004-09}}</ref> ). It is called ``Shoten-sama (of Menuma)'' by worshipers and local residents.

=== History ===
According to temple legend, in the 3rd year of Jisho ({{ill|lt=1179|Q19698|WD=Q19698|1=1179}}), the military commander {{ill|lt=Sanemori Saito|Q3472140|WD=Q3472140|lt=It is said that Fujibetsuto Sanemori|1=Sanemori Saitō}} built Shotengu Shrine to enshrine the guardian deity Daisei {{ill|lt=Kankiten|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315|1=Kangiten}} (Shoten) and made it the general guardian of Nagaisho. Later, in the 8th year of Kenkyu (1197), Ryo'o Sozu (Sanenaga, the second son of Saito Betto Sanemori) built Kangi-in Choraku-ji Temple as the Betto temple (honbo) of Shotengu Shrine, and it is said that {{ill|lt=Eleven-faced Kannon|Q11404731|WD=Q11404731|1=Ekādaśamukha}} was the principal image.

{{ill|lt=Kamakura Shogunate|Q736839|WD=Q736839|1=Kamakura shogunate}}'s first shogun, {{ill|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|WD=Q242800|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, visited the shrine, and in the medieval period it was protected by the lord of Oshi Castle, and in the early modern period it was rebuilt by {{ill|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|WD=Q171977|1=Tokugawa Ieyasu}}, but it was destroyed by the Great Menuma Fire in 1670. The current Shotendo (main shrine) was rebuilt between the Kyoho and Horeki eras (mid-18th century).

Restoration work on the main shrine was carried out from 2003 to 2011, and the completion ceremony for the main building was held on January 18, 2010, and the completion ceremony was held on June 1, 2011, and it opened to the public on the same day. On July 9, 2012, Seitendo (main shrine) was designated as a {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} (the first designation as a National Treasure building in Saitama Prefecture).

=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
; Seitendo (main hall)
: It is a mausoleum-style {{ill|lt=Gongen-zukuri|Q3155268|WD=Q3155268|1=Ishi-no-ma-zukuri}} building (an architectural style that combines multiple buildings, as seen in Nikko Toshogu Shrine, etc.), which consists of a worship hall, a middle hall (so-ma), and a back hall. The master carpenter was the master carpenter Hayashi Hyogo Masakiyo of Menuma, a descendant of {{ill|lt=Masanobu Hiranai|Q11482097|WD=Q11482097|1=Heinouchi Masanobu}}, the master carpenter of the shogunate.The building was rebuilt over a period of more than 20 years, from 1735 to 1760, by his son Masanobu. The inner hall is a gambrel-style structure with 3 girders and 3 girders, with a front facing prayer hall.The middle hall is Ryosage-zukuri, with 3 girder rows and 1 girder.The worship hall is gambrel-style, with 5 girder rows and 3 beams.These are connected to form a single building, and the roof is all roofed with tile-rod copper plates.: The inner and outer halls are highly decorative with splendid carvings, lacquering, coloring, metal fittings, etc. both inside and outside. The ``eagle and monkey'' carvings on the paneling on the south side of the inner hall are said to have been created by the legendary carving craftsman {{ill|lt=Hidashi Jingoro|Q2668220|WD=Q2668220|1=Hidari Jingorō}}, but the actual master carvers were Ginpachiro Ishihara (Ginpachi) and Bunjiro Sekiguchi. In the inner hall, the pillars, pushpieces, and other members are carved with ground patterns, and the large paneling under the inner law is decorated with the Seven Lucky Gods, and the area under the rim is decorated with colored carvings depicting the theme of playing with karako. Each of the carvings has a theme related to a Chinese story, such as ``Three Saints' Susan'' and ``{{ill|lt=Sima Guang|Q33566|WD=Q33566|lt=Sima Wengong|1=Sima Guang}}'s Bottle Breaker'' under the kara gable, and ``Kotogi Calligraphy'' under the kara gable in front of the shrine. Repairs were carried out from 2003 to 2010, mainly re-roofing and coloring, and the original coloring was restored. Designated as {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} in 2012<ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.bunka.go.jp/ima/press_release/pdf/jubunkenzou_shittei_240521.pdf About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) (Agency for Cultural Affairs)]}}</ref>{{deadurl|date=July 2018}}<ref>Designation of National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties (Buildings) in 2012 ○From National Treasures (Buildings){{Cite book|Japanese book|title= White Paper on Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Chapter 8 Part 2 / Trends and developments in education, science and technology policies - Realizing a nation built on culture and the arts |chapter=Designated on July 9, 2012 (1 item in total) Kangi-in Seitendo |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/hakusho/html/hpab201301/1338525_019.pdf|format = PDF |page= 294|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2018-07-10}}</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 106 of July 9, 2012</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url= http://www.city.kumagaya.lg.jp/kanko/midokoro/menumasyoudenzan/kangiinkokuho.html |title=“Kangi-in Seitendo” designated as a national treasure|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2012-07-12|publisher= Kumagaya City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|Japanese book|others= Cultural Properties Protection Committee; Agency for Cultural Affairs Cultural Properties Protection Department |title = Newly designated cultural properties |work= Monthly cultural properties |publisher = Daiichi Hoki Publishing |number= 586|year = 2012|issn= 0016-5948 |ncid= AN00221652}}</ref>.

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
[[File:Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|The statues of Kangiten and Two Doji are cast in the center. ]]
*Kisomon - An 18m high copper plate roofed eight-legged gate located at the front entrance of the temple grounds. This unique gate has a double roof, upper and lower, with two gable roofs at the front and back, and when viewed from the side, has three gables. Statues of Jikokuten and Tamonten are placed on the left and right. It was built by Masamichi Hayashi of Menuma in the 4th year of the Kaei era, and completed around 1855.
*Shakujoto - The secret principal image of Buddha in Shotendo. There is an inscription dating back to 1197, and the statues of Kangiten and Nidoji are cast in the center. A shakujo is a staff held by Jizo Bodhisattva and others, and the head of the staff sometimes represents a Buddha statue.

=== Inarizushi in Menuma ===
[[File:Menuma Inari-zushi 01.JPG|thumb|200px|Menuma Inari-zushi]]
It has been eaten since the Edo period, mainly by visitors to our hospital. Kumagaya City Tourism Association official website|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, {{ill|lt=Inari sushi|Q874397|WD=Q874397|1=Inarizushi}} is a specialty of the Menuma district (formerly {{ill|lt=Menuma Town|Q6817684|WD=Q6817684|1=Menuma, Saitama}}). It is characterized by its elongated shape, which is different from typical Inari sushi.Before the war, on the contrary, this elongated shape was common, but after the war, with the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=contract processing system|1=UNKNOWN}}, the standard was reduced to the size of nigiri sushi. However, in the Menuma area, efforts were made to maintain the elongated shape, resulting in the sushi being a specialty that continues to this day. To be a "jumbo"...Submit a report and keep the size Kumagaya's Jumbo Inari "100 Year Food" certification report meeting (Saitama Shimbun) - Yahoo! News]</ref>. In recent years, it has become popular as a specialty attached to the national treasure (main shrine).

{{ill|lt=Maki sushi|Q5739461|WD=Q5739461|1=Makizushi}} Three sushi restaurants specialize in this set (Sukeroku sushi), all of which originated as the teahouse in front of our hospital. <ref name=":0" /> operates within the hospital grounds and nearby areas. Similar products can also be found in surrounding areas, such as {{ill|lt=Roadside Station Menuma|Q11640968|WD=Q11640968|1=Roadside station Menuma}}'s ``{{ill|lt=Ginko Ogino|Q4794092|WD=Q4794092|lt=Gingin|1=Ogino Ginko}} Sushi.''On {{ill|lt=Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|Q1376786|WD=Q1376786|1=Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (Japan)}}'s "My Local Cuisine" website, it is introduced under the name "Shoten Sushi", which originates from our hospital.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shoten Sushi Saitama Prefecture {{!}} Our local cuisine: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|url=https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/33_29_saitama.html|website=www.maff.go.jp|access-date=2026-01-17}}</ref> etc.<ref group="Note">It is also sometimes written as "Shoten Sushi". It is presumed that all of these names are misspelled from the shop name <!-- Shoten Sushi --> of the three shops mentioned above, which faces the temple grounds, and it seems inappropriate as a unified name for the three shops. </ref>In the past, there was no unified name, but as a tourist guide for Kumagaya City, it was advertised under the name ``''Menuma no Inarizushi''. Kumagaya City Tourism Association Official Homepage|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, as this name has also been applied and registered in the 100-year food program mentioned below, in recent years, each of the 4 “Nagai Inari Sushi from the Menuma area” products, including Gingin Sushi, have been introduced.<ref name=":0" It is common to refer to the general term ``'''Menuma no Inarizushi''''.March 3, 2023, {{ill|lt=Agency for Cultural Affairs|Q1009519|WD=Q1009519|1=Agency for Cultural Affairs}} “{{ill|lt=100 Years of Food|Q134383966|WD=Q134383966|1=100 Years of Food}}” “100 Years of Traditional Food Category ～Local cuisine that has continued since the Edo period～” <ref>[https://foodculture2021.go.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/r4_100nenfood.pdf List of “100 Year Food” by prefecture (FY2020)]</ref>.

=== Transportation ===

=== car ===
*{{ill|lt=Gunma Prefectural Road/Saitama Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line|Q11609884|WD=Q11609884|lt=Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line|1=Gunma Prefectural Road and Saitama Prefectural Road Route 341}} Along. In addition, between the main hall and the main temple, {{ill|lt=Saitama Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumuma Line|Q11427072|WD=Q11427072|lt=Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumanum Line|1=Saitama Prefectural Road Route 59}} runs, and is called ``Enmusubi Dori'' (because this hospital is said to have {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=divine blessings|1=UNKNOWN}} for matchmaking).
*: There is a private parking lot nearby. However, the parking spaces facing the approach between the Ota Kumagaya Line and Kisomon Gate and the 6th parking lot behind the main shrine are not available for use by worshipers (please refer to the official website and local information).
*: Since the shrine is crowded during New Year's holidays and during spring and autumn festivals, Kumagaya City recommends parking at the Menuma Tourist Parking Lot in the south and taking a stroll around the shrine.

=== Bus ===
*{{ill|lt=Asahi Motors|Q11517584|WD=Q11517584|lt=Asahi Bus|1=Asahi Motor}}: {{ill|lt=Kumagaya Station|Q735594|WD=Q735594|1=Kumagaya Station}} North Exit Platform 6 - [KM61] {{ill|lt=Ota Station (Gunma Prefecture)|Q8081729|WD=Q8081729|lt=Ota Station|1=Ōta Station (Gunma)}} line/[KM63] Take the bus bound for {{ill|lt=Nishikoizumi Station|Q11627702|WD=Q11627702|1=Nishi-Koizumi Station}}/[KM64] Menuma Shotenmae<ref group="Notes">[KM65] Menuma, get off at the "Menuma Shimomachi" stop, and walk for 13 minutes. </ref>, get off at the "Menuma Shoten-mae" stop. *Late-night hours after 10pm depart from bus stop 3 (destinations above + [KM62] bound for Nishiyajima are also available)
*{{ill|lt=Yu-Yu Bus (Kumagaya City)|Q11280693|WD=Q11280693|lt=Yu-Yu Bus|1=Kumagaya City Community Bus}} (Community Bus): Glider (Kumagaya Station South Exit - Menuma Administrative Center), Glider Wagon (Menuma Circulation), get off at the "Menuma Shoten-mae" stop or the "Shotenzan Minami Entrance" stop.

[[File:Kisoumon.jpg|thumb|240px|Kisoumon]]'''Kangiin'' is {{ill|lt=Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|WD=Q128186|1=Saitama Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Kumagaya City|Q41106|WD=Q41106|1=Kumagaya}}{{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684| It is {{ill|lt=Buddhism|Q748|WD=Q748|1=Buddhism}}{{ill|lt=temple|Q5393308|WD=Q5393308|1=Buddhist temple}} of {{ill|lt=Koyasan Shingon sect|Q3077357|WD=Q3077357|1=Kōyasan Shingon-shū}} located in Menuma}}. {{ill|lt=Kankiten#Japan's three great holy deities|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315|lt=Japan's three great holy deities|1=Kangiten}} It is generally referred to as ``Menuma Shodenzan,'' which is a place name attached to the mountain name, and is mainly used in official guides.
Also, "Saitama {{ill|lt=Nikko Toshogu|Q696641|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikko|1=Nikkō Tōshō-gū}}" (before it was designated as a national treasure, it was "Saitama's Konikko") |publisher= local publisher |isbn= 4-87663-703-2 |date= 2004-09}}</ref> ). It is called ``Shoten-sama (of Menuma)'' by worshipers and local residents.

=== History ===
According to temple legend, in the 3rd year of Jisho ({{ill|lt=1179|Q19698|WD=Q19698|1=1179}}), the military commander {{ill|lt=Sanemori Saito|Q3472140|WD=Q3472140|lt=It is said that Fujibetsuto Sanemori|1=Sanemori Saitō}} built Shotengu Shrine to enshrine the guardian deity Daisei {{ill|lt=Kankiten|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315|1=Kangiten}} (Shoten) and made it the general guardian of Nagaisho. Later, in the 8th year of Kenkyu (1197), Ryo'o Sozu (Sanenaga, the second son of Saito Betto Sanemori) built Kangi-in Choraku-ji Temple as the Betto temple (honbo) of Shotengu Shrine, and it is said that {{ill|lt=Eleven-faced Kannon|Q11404731|WD=Q11404731|1=Ekādaśamukha}} was the principal image.

{{ill|lt=Kamakura Shogunate|Q736839|WD=Q736839|1=Kamakura shogunate}}'s first shogun, {{ill|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|WD=Q242800|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, visited the shrine, and in the medieval period it was protected by the lord of Oshi Castle, and in the early modern period it was rebuilt by {{ill|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|WD=Q171977|1=Tokugawa Ieyasu}}, but it was destroyed by the Great Menuma Fire in 1670. The current Shotendo (main shrine) was rebuilt between the Kyoho and Horeki eras (mid-18th century).

Restoration work on the main shrine was carried out from 2003 to 2011, and the completion ceremony for the main building was held on January 18, 2010, and the completion ceremony was held on June 1, 2011, and it opened to the public on the same day. On July 9, 2012, Seitendo (main shrine) was designated as a {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} (the first designation as a National Treasure building in Saitama Prefecture).

=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
; Seitendo (main hall)
: It is a mausoleum-style {{ill|lt=Gongen-zukuri|Q3155268|WD=Q3155268|1=Ishi-no-ma-zukuri}} building (an architectural style that combines multiple buildings, as seen in Nikko Toshogu Shrine, etc.), which consists of a worship hall, a middle hall (so-ma), and a back hall. The master carpenter was the master carpenter Hayashi Hyogo Masakiyo of Menuma, a descendant of {{ill|lt=Masanobu Hiranai|Q11482097|WD=Q11482097|1=Heinouchi Masanobu}}, the master carpenter of the shogunate.The building was rebuilt over a period of more than 20 years, from 1735 to 1760, by his son Masanobu. The inner hall is a gambrel-style structure with 3 girders and 3 girders, with a front facing prayer hall.The middle hall is Ryosage-zukuri, with 3 girder rows and 1 girder.The worship hall is gambrel-style, with 5 girder rows and 3 beams.These are connected to form a single building, and the roof is all roofed with tile-rod copper plates.: The inner and outer halls are highly decorative with splendid carvings, lacquering, coloring, metal fittings, etc. both inside and outside. The ``eagle and monkey'' carvings on the paneling on the south side of the inner hall are said to have been created by the legendary carving craftsman {{ill|lt=Hidashi Jingoro|Q2668220|WD=Q2668220|1=Hidari Jingorō}}, but the actual master carvers were Ginpachiro Ishihara (Ginpachi) and Bunjiro Sekiguchi. In the inner hall, the pillars, pushpieces, and other members are carved with ground patterns, and the large paneling under the inner law is decorated with the Seven Lucky Gods, and the area under the rim is decorated with colored carvings depicting the theme of playing with karako. Each of the carvings has a theme related to a Chinese story, such as ``Three Saints' Susan'' and ``{{ill|lt=Sima Guang|Q33566|WD=Q33566|lt=Sima Wengong|1=Sima Guang}}'s Bottle Breaker'' under the kara gable, and ``Kotogi Calligraphy'' under the kara gable in front of the shrine. Repairs were carried out from 2003 to 2010, mainly re-roofing and coloring, and the original coloring was restored. Designated as {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} in 2012<ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.bunka.go.jp/ima/press_release/pdf/jubunkenzou_shittei_240521.pdf About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) (Agency for Cultural Affairs)]}}</ref>{{deadurl|date=July 2018}}<ref>Designation of National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties (Buildings) in 2012 ○From National Treasures (Buildings){{Cite book|Japanese book|title= White Paper on Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Chapter 8 Part 2 / Trends and developments in education, science and technology policies - Realizing a nation built on culture and the arts |chapter=Designated on July 9, 2012 (1 item in total) Kangi-in Seitendo |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/hakusho/html/hpab201301/1338525_019.pdf|format = PDF |page= 294|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2018-07-10}}</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 106 of July 9, 2012</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url= http://www.city.kumagaya.lg.jp/kanko/midokoro/menumasyoudenzan/kangiinkokuho.html |title=“Kangi-in Seitendo” designated as a national treasure|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2012-07-12|publisher= Kumagaya City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|Japanese book|others= Cultural Properties Protection Committee; Agency for Cultural Affairs Cultural Properties Protection Department |title = Newly designated cultural properties |work= Monthly cultural properties |publisher = Daiichi Hoki Publishing |number= 586|year = 2012|issn= 0016-5948 |ncid= AN00221652}}</ref>.

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
[[File:Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|The statues of Kangiten and Two Doji are cast in the center. ]]
*Kisomon - An 18m high copper plate roofed eight-legged gate located at the front entrance of the temple grounds. This unique gate has a double roof, upper and lower, with two gable roofs at the front and back, and when viewed from the side, has three gables. Statues of Jikokuten and Tamonten are placed on the left and right. It was built by Masamichi Hayashi of Menuma in the 4th year of the Kaei era, and completed around 1855.
*Shakujoto - The secret principal image of Buddha in Shotendo. There is an inscription dating back to 1197, and the statues of Kangiten and Nidoji are cast in the center. A shakujo is a staff held by Jizo Bodhisattva and others, and the head of the staff sometimes represents a Buddha statue.

=== Inarizushi in Menuma ===
[[File:Menuma Inari-zushi 01.JPG|thumb|200px|Menuma Inari-zushi]]
It has been eaten since the Edo period, mainly by visitors to our hospital. Kumagaya City Tourism Association official website|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, {{ill|lt=Inari sushi|Q874397|WD=Q874397|1=Inarizushi}} is a specialty of the Menuma district (formerly {{ill|lt=Menuma Town|Q6817684|WD=Q6817684|1=Menuma, Saitama}}). It is characterized by its elongated shape, which is different from typical Inari sushi.Before the war, on the contrary, this elongated shape was common, but after the war, with the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=contract processing system|1=UNKNOWN}}, the standard was reduced to the size of nigiri sushi. However, in the Menuma area, efforts were made to maintain the elongated shape, resulting in the sushi being a specialty that continues to this day. To be a "jumbo"...Submit a report and keep the size Kumagaya's Jumbo Inari "100 Year Food" certification report meeting (Saitama Shimbun) - Yahoo! News]</ref>. In recent years, it has become popular as a specialty attached to the national treasure (main shrine).

{{ill|lt=Maki sushi|Q5739461|WD=Q5739461|1=Makizushi}} Three sushi restaurants specialize in this set (Sukeroku sushi), all of which originated as the teahouse in front of our hospital. <ref name=":0" /> operates within the hospital grounds and nearby areas. Similar products can also be found in surrounding areas, such as {{ill|lt=Roadside Station Menuma|Q11640968|WD=Q11640968|1=Roadside station Menuma}}'s ``{{ill|lt=Ginko Ogino|Q4794092|WD=Q4794092|lt=Gingin|1=Ogino Ginko}} Sushi.''On {{ill|lt=Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|Q1376786|WD=Q1376786|1=Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (Japan)}}'s "My Local Cuisine" website, it is introduced under the name "Shoten Sushi", which originates from our hospital.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shoten Sushi Saitama Prefecture {{!}} Our local cuisine: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|url=https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/33_29_saitama.html|website=www.maff.go.jp|access-date=2026-01-17}}</ref> etc.<ref group="Note">It is also sometimes written as "Shoten Sushi". It is presumed that all of these names are misspelled from the shop name <!-- Shoten Sushi --> of the three shops mentioned above, which faces the temple grounds, and it seems inappropriate as a unified name for the three shops. </ref>In the past, there was no unified name, but as a tourist guide for Kumagaya City, it was advertised under the name ``''Menuma no Inarizushi''. Kumagaya City Tourism Association Official Homepage|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, as this name has also been applied and registered in the 100-year food program mentioned below, in recent years, each of the 4 “Nagai Inari Sushi from the Menuma area” products, including Gingin Sushi, have been introduced.<ref name=":0" It is common to refer to the general term ``'''Menuma no Inarizushi''''.March 3, 2023, {{ill|lt=Agency for Cultural Affairs|Q1009519|WD=Q1009519|1=Agency for Cultural Affairs}} “{{ill|lt=100 Years of Food|Q134383966|WD=Q134383966|1=100 Years of Food}}” “100 Years of Traditional Food Category ～Local cuisine that has continued since the Edo period～” <ref>[https://foodculture2021.go.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/r4_100nenfood.pdf List of “100 Year Food” by prefecture (FY2020)]</ref>.

[[File:Kisoumon.jpg|thumb|240px|Kisoumon]]'''Kangiin'' is {{ill|lt=Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|WD=Q128186|1=Saitama Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Kumagaya City|Q41106|WD=Q41106|1=Kumagaya}}{{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684| It is {{ill|lt=Buddhism|Q748|WD=Q748|1=Buddhism}}{{ill|lt=temple|Q5393308|WD=Q5393308|1=Buddhist temple}} of {{ill|lt=Koyasan Shingon sect|Q3077357|WD=Q3077357|1=Kōyasan Shingon-shū}} located in Menuma}}. {{ill|lt=Kankiten#Japan's three great holy deities|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315|lt=Japan's three great holy deities|1=Kangiten}} It is generally referred to as ``Menuma Shodenzan,'' which is a place name attached to the mountain name, and is mainly used in official guides.
Also, "Saitama {{ill|lt=Nikko Toshogu|Q696641|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikko|1=Nikkō Tōshō-gū}}" (before it was designated as a national treasure, it was "Saitama's Konikko") |publisher= local publisher |isbn= 4-87663-703-2 |date= 2004-09}}</ref> ). It is called ``Shoten-sama (of Menuma)'' by worshipers and local residents.

=== History ===
According to temple legend, in the 3rd year of Jisho ({{ill|lt=1179|Q19698|WD=Q19698|1=1179}}), the military commander {{ill|lt=Sanemori Saito|Q3472140|WD=Q3472140|lt=It is said that Fujibetsuto Sanemori|1=Sanemori Saitō}} built Shotengu Shrine to enshrine the guardian deity Daisei {{ill|lt=Kankiten|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315|1=Kangiten}} (Shoten) and made it the general guardian of Nagaisho. Later, in the 8th year of Kenkyu (1197), Ryo'o Sozu (Sanenaga, the second son of Saito Betto Sanemori) built Kangi-in Choraku-ji Temple as the Betto temple (honbo) of Shotengu Shrine, and it is said that {{ill|lt=Eleven-faced Kannon|Q11404731|WD=Q11404731|1=Ekādaśamukha}} was the principal image.

{{ill|lt=Kamakura Shogunate|Q736839|WD=Q736839|1=Kamakura shogunate}}'s first shogun, {{ill|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|WD=Q242800|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, visited the shrine, and in the medieval period it was protected by the lord of Oshi Castle, and in the early modern period it was rebuilt by {{ill|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|WD=Q171977|1=Tokugawa Ieyasu}}, but it was destroyed by the Great Menuma Fire in 1670. The current Shotendo (main shrine) was rebuilt between the Kyoho and Horeki eras (mid-18th century).

Restoration work on the main shrine was carried out from 2003 to 2011, and the completion ceremony for the main building was held on January 18, 2010, and the completion ceremony was held on June 1, 2011, and it opened to the public on the same day. On July 9, 2012, Seitendo (main shrine) was designated as a {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} (the first designation as a National Treasure building in Saitama Prefecture).

=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
; Seitendo (main hall)
: It is a mausoleum-style {{ill|lt=Gongen-zukuri|Q3155268|WD=Q3155268|1=Ishi-no-ma-zukuri}} building (an architectural style that combines multiple buildings, as seen in Nikko Toshogu Shrine, etc.), which consists of a worship hall, a middle hall (so-ma), and a back hall. The master carpenter was the master carpenter Hayashi Hyogo Masakiyo of Menuma, a descendant of {{ill|lt=Masanobu Hiranai|Q11482097|WD=Q11482097|1=Heinouchi Masanobu}}, the master carpenter of the shogunate.The building was rebuilt over a period of more than 20 years, from 1735 to 1760, by his son Masanobu. The inner hall is a gambrel-style structure with 3 girders and 3 girders, with a front facing prayer hall.The middle hall is Ryosage-zukuri, with 3 girder rows and 1 girder.The worship hall is gambrel-style, with 5 girder rows and 3 beams.These are connected to form a single building, and the roof is all roofed with tile-rod copper plates.: The inner and outer halls are highly decorative with splendid carvings, lacquering, coloring, metal fittings, etc. both inside and outside. The ``eagle and monkey'' carvings on the paneling on the south side of the inner hall are said to have been created by the legendary carving craftsman {{ill|lt=Hidashi Jingoro|Q2668220|WD=Q2668220|1=Hidari Jingorō}}, but the actual master carvers were Ginpachiro Ishihara (Ginpachi) and Bunjiro Sekiguchi. In the inner hall, the pillars, pushpieces, and other members are carved with ground patterns, and the large paneling under the inner law is decorated with the Seven Lucky Gods, and the area under the rim is decorated with colored carvings depicting the theme of playing with karako. Each of the carvings has a theme related to a Chinese story, such as ``Three Saints' Susan'' and ``{{ill|lt=Sima Guang|Q33566|WD=Q33566|lt=Sima Wengong|1=Sima Guang}}'s Bottle Breaker'' under the kara gable, and ``Kotogi Calligraphy'' under the kara gable in front of the shrine. Repairs were carried out from 2003 to 2010, mainly re-roofing and coloring, and the original coloring was restored. Designated as {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} in 2012<ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.bunka.go.jp/ima/press_release/pdf/jubunkenzou_shittei_240521.pdf About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) (Agency for Cultural Affairs)]}}</ref>{{deadurl|date=July 2018}}<ref>Designation of National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties (Buildings) in 2012 ○From National Treasures (Buildings){{Cite book|Japanese book|title= White Paper on Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Chapter 8 Part 2 / Trends and developments in education, science and technology policies - Realizing a nation built on culture and the arts |chapter=Designated on July 9, 2012 (1 item in total) Kangi-in Seitendo |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/hakusho/html/hpab201301/1338525_019.pdf|format = PDF |page= 294|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2018-07-10}}</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 106 of July 9, 2012</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url= http://www.city.kumagaya.lg.jp/kanko/midokoro/menumasyoudenzan/kangiinkokuho.html |title=“Kangi-in Seitendo” designated as a national treasure|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2012-07-12|publisher= Kumagaya City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|Japanese book|others= Cultural Properties Protection Committee; Agency for Cultural Affairs Cultural Properties Protection Department |title = Newly designated cultural properties |work= Monthly cultural properties |publisher = Daiichi Hoki Publishing |number= 586|year = 2012|issn= 0016-5948 |ncid= AN00221652}}</ref>.

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
[[File:Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|The statues of Kangiten and Two Doji are cast in the center. ]]
*Kisomon - An 18m high copper plate roofed eight-legged gate located at the front entrance of the temple grounds. This unique gate has a double roof, upper and lower, with two gable roofs at the front and back, and when viewed from the side, has three gables. Statues of Jikokuten and Tamonten are placed on the left and right. It was built by Masamichi Hayashi of Menuma in the 4th year of the Kaei era, and completed around 1855.
*Shakujoto - The secret principal image of Buddha in Shotendo. There is an inscription dating back to 1197, and the statues of Kangiten and Nidoji are cast in the center. A shakujo is a staff held by Jizo Bodhisattva and others, and the head of the staff sometimes represents a Buddha statue.

=== Inarizushi in Menuma ===
[[File:Menuma Inari-zushi 01.JPG|thumb|200px|Menuma Inari-zushi]]
It has been eaten since the Edo period, mainly by visitors to our hospital. Kumagaya City Tourism Association official website|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, {{ill|lt=Inari sushi|Q874397|WD=Q874397|1=Inarizushi}} is a specialty of the Menuma district (formerly {{ill|lt=Menuma Town|Q6817684|WD=Q6817684|1=Menuma, Saitama}}). It is characterized by its elongated shape, which is different from typical Inari sushi.Before the war, on the contrary, this elongated shape was common, but after the war, with the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=contract processing system|1=UNKNOWN}}, the standard was reduced to the size of nigiri sushi. However, in the Menuma area, efforts were made to maintain the elongated shape, resulting in the sushi being a specialty that continues to this day. To be a "jumbo"...Submit a report and keep the size Kumagaya's Jumbo Inari "100 Year Food" certification report meeting (Saitama Shimbun) - Yahoo! News]</ref>. In recent years, it has become popular as a specialty attached to the national treasure (main shrine).

{{ill|lt=Maki sushi|Q5739461|WD=Q5739461|1=Makizushi}} Three sushi restaurants specialize in this set (Sukeroku sushi), all of which originated as the teahouse in front of our hospital. <ref name=":0" /> operates within the hospital grounds and nearby areas. Similar products can also be found in surrounding areas, such as {{ill|lt=Roadside Station Menuma|Q11640968|WD=Q11640968|1=Roadside station Menuma}}'s ``{{ill|lt=Ginko Ogino|Q4794092|WD=Q4794092|lt=Gingin|1=Ogino Ginko}} Sushi.''On {{ill|lt=Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|Q1376786|WD=Q1376786|1=Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (Japan)}}'s "My Local Cuisine" website, it is introduced under the name "Shoten Sushi", which originates from our hospital.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shoten Sushi Saitama Prefecture {{!}} Our local cuisine: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries|url=https://www.maff.go.jp/j/keikaku/syokubunka/k_ryouri/search_menu/menu/33_29_saitama.html|website=www.maff.go.jp|access-date=2026-01-17}}</ref> etc.<ref group="Note">It is also sometimes written as "Shoten Sushi". It is presumed that all of these names are misspelled from the shop name <!-- Shoten Sushi --> of the three shops mentioned above, which faces the temple grounds, and it seems inappropriate as a unified name for the three shops. </ref>In the past, there was no unified name, but as a tourist guide for Kumagaya City, it was advertised under the name ``''Menuma no Inarizushi''. Kumagaya City Tourism Association Official Homepage|date=2014-10-02|access-date=2026-01-17|last=}}</ref>, as this name has also been applied and registered in the 100-year food program mentioned below, in recent years, each of the 4 “Nagai Inari Sushi from the Menuma area” products, including Gingin Sushi, have been introduced.<ref name=":0" It is common to refer to the general term ``'''Menuma no Inarizushi''''.March 3, 2023, {{ill|lt=Agency for Cultural Affairs|Q1009519|WD=Q1009519|1=Agency for Cultural Affairs}} “{{ill|lt=100 Years of Food|Q134383966|WD=Q134383966|1=100 Years of Food}}” “100 Years of Traditional Food Category ～Local cuisine that has continued since the Edo period～” <ref>[https://foodculture2021.go.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/r4_100nenfood.pdf List of “100 Year Food” by prefecture (FY2020)]</ref>.

=== Transportation ===

=== car ===
*{{ill|lt=Gunma Prefectural Road/Saitama Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line|Q11609884|WD=Q11609884|lt=Prefectural Road No. 341 Ota Kumagaya Line|1=Gunma Prefectural Road and Saitama Prefectural Road Route 341}} Along. In addition, between the main hall and the main temple, {{ill|lt=Saitama Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumuma Line|Q11427072|WD=Q11427072|lt=Prefectural Road No. 59 Hanyu-Tsumanum Line|1=Saitama Prefectural Road Route 59}} runs, and is called ``Enmusubi Dori'' (because this hospital is said to have {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=divine blessings|1=UNKNOWN}} for matchmaking).
*: There is a private parking lot nearby. However, the parking spaces facing the approach between the Ota Kumagaya Line and Kisomon Gate and the 6th parking lot behind the main shrine are not available for use by worshipers (please refer to the official website and local information).
*: Since the shrine is crowded during New Year's holidays and during spring and autumn festivals, Kumagaya City recommends parking at the Menuma Tourist Parking Lot in the south and taking a stroll around the shrine.

=== Bus ===
*{{ill|lt=Asahi Motors|Q11517584|WD=Q11517584|lt=Asahi Bus|1=Asahi Motor}}: {{ill|lt=Kumagaya Station|Q735594|WD=Q735594|1=Kumagaya Station}} North Exit Platform 6 - [KM61] {{ill|lt=Ota Station (Gunma Prefecture)|Q8081729|WD=Q8081729|lt=Ota Station|1=Ōta Station (Gunma)}} line/[KM63] Take the bus bound for {{ill|lt=Nishikoizumi Station|Q11627702|WD=Q11627702|1=Nishi-Koizumi Station}}/[KM64] Menuma Shotenmae<ref group="Notes">[KM65] Menuma, get off at the "Menuma Shimomachi" stop, and walk for 13 minutes. </ref>, get off at the "Menuma Shoten-mae" stop. *Late-night hours after 10pm depart from bus stop 3 (destinations above + [KM62] bound for Nishiyajima are also available)
*{{ill|lt=Yu-Yu Bus (Kumagaya City)|Q11280693|WD=Q11280693|lt=Yu-Yu Bus|1=Kumagaya City Community Bus}} (Community Bus): Glider (Kumagaya Station South Exit - Menuma Administrative Center), Glider Wagon (Menuma Circulation), get off at the "Menuma Shoten-mae" stop or the "Shotenzan Minami Entrance" stop.

[[File:Kisoumon.jpg|thumb|240px|Kisoumon]]'''Kangiin'' is {{ill|lt=Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|WD=Q128186|1=Saitama Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Kumagaya City|Q41106|WD=Q41106|1=Kumagaya}}{{jalink|Menuma Town|Q6817684| It is {{ill|lt=Buddhism|Q748|WD=Q748|1=Buddhism}}{{ill|lt=temple|Q5393308|WD=Q5393308|1=Buddhist temple}} of {{ill|lt=Koyasan Shingon sect|Q3077357|WD=Q3077357|1=Kōyasan Shingon-shū}} located in Menuma}}. {{ill|lt=Kankiten#Japan's three great holy deities|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315|lt=Japan's three great holy deities|1=Kangiten}} It is generally referred to as ``Menuma Shodenzan,'' which is a place name attached to the mountain name, and is mainly used in official guides.
Also, "Saitama {{ill|lt=Nikko Toshogu|Q696641|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikko|1=Nikkō Tōshō-gū}}" (before it was designated as a national treasure, it was "Saitama's Konikko") |publisher= local publisher |isbn= 4-87663-703-2 |date= 2004-09}}</ref> ). It is called ``Shoten-sama (of Menuma)'' by worshipers and local residents.

=== History ===
According to temple legend, in the 3rd year of Jisho ({{ill|lt=1179|Q19698|WD=Q19698|1=1179}}), the military commander {{ill|lt=Sanemori Saito|Q3472140|WD=Q3472140|lt=It is said that Fujibetsuto Sanemori|1=Sanemori Saitō}} built Shotengu Shrine to enshrine the guardian deity Daisei {{ill|lt=Kankiten|Q11545315|WD=Q11545315|1=Kangiten}} (Shoten) and made it the general guardian of Nagaisho. Later, in the 8th year of Kenkyu (1197), Ryo'o Sozu (Sanenaga, the second son of Saito Betto Sanemori) built Kangi-in Choraku-ji Temple as the Betto temple (honbo) of Shotengu Shrine, and it is said that {{ill|lt=Eleven-faced Kannon|Q11404731|WD=Q11404731|1=Ekādaśamukha}} was the principal image.

{{ill|lt=Kamakura Shogunate|Q736839|WD=Q736839|1=Kamakura shogunate}}'s first shogun, {{ill|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|WD=Q242800|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, visited the shrine, and in the medieval period it was protected by the lord of Oshi Castle, and in the early modern period it was rebuilt by {{ill|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|WD=Q171977|1=Tokugawa Ieyasu}}, but it was destroyed by the Great Menuma Fire in 1670. The current Shotendo (main shrine) was rebuilt between the Kyoho and Horeki eras (mid-18th century).

Restoration work on the main shrine was carried out from 2003 to 2011, and the completion ceremony for the main building was held on January 18, 2010, and the completion ceremony was held on June 1, 2011, and it opened to the public on the same day. On July 9, 2012, Seitendo (main shrine) was designated as a {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} (the first designation as a National Treasure building in Saitama Prefecture).

=== Cultural assets ===

=== National Treasure ===
; Seitendo (main hall)
: It is a mausoleum-style {{ill|lt=Gongen-zukuri|Q3155268|WD=Q3155268|1=Ishi-no-ma-zukuri}} building (an architectural style that combines multiple buildings, as seen in Nikko Toshogu Shrine, etc.), which consists of a worship hall, a middle hall (so-ma), and a back hall. The master carpenter was the master carpenter Hayashi Hyogo Masakiyo of Menuma, a descendant of {{ill|lt=Masanobu Hiranai|Q11482097|WD=Q11482097|1=Heinouchi Masanobu}}, the master carpenter of the shogunate.The building was rebuilt over a period of more than 20 years, from 1735 to 1760, by his son Masanobu. The inner hall is a gambrel-style structure with 3 girders and 3 girders, with a front facing prayer hall.The middle hall is Ryosage-zukuri, with 3 girder rows and 1 girder.The worship hall is gambrel-style, with 5 girder rows and 3 beams.These are connected to form a single building, and the roof is all roofed with tile-rod copper plates.: The inner and outer halls are highly decorative with splendid carvings, lacquering, coloring, metal fittings, etc. both inside and outside. The ``eagle and monkey'' carvings on the paneling on the south side of the inner hall are said to have been created by the legendary carving craftsman {{ill|lt=Hidashi Jingoro|Q2668220|WD=Q2668220|1=Hidari Jingorō}}, but the actual master carvers were Ginpachiro Ishihara (Ginpachi) and Bunjiro Sekiguchi. In the inner hall, the pillars, pushpieces, and other members are carved with ground patterns, and the large paneling under the inner law is decorated with the Seven Lucky Gods, and the area under the rim is decorated with colored carvings depicting the theme of playing with karako. Each of the carvings has a theme related to a Chinese story, such as ``Three Saints' Susan'' and ``{{ill|lt=Sima Guang|Q33566|WD=Q33566|lt=Sima Wengong|1=Sima Guang}}'s Bottle Breaker'' under the kara gable, and ``Kotogi Calligraphy'' under the kara gable in front of the shrine. Repairs were carried out from 2003 to 2010, mainly re-roofing and coloring, and the original coloring was restored. Designated as {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} in 2012<ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.bunka.go.jp/ima/press_release/pdf/jubunkenzou_shittei_240521.pdf About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) (Agency for Cultural Affairs)]}}</ref>{{deadurl|date=July 2018}}<ref>Designation of National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties (Buildings) in 2012 ○From National Treasures (Buildings){{Cite book|Japanese book|title= White Paper on Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Chapter 8 Part 2 / Trends and developments in education, science and technology policies - Realizing a nation built on culture and the arts |chapter=Designated on July 9, 2012 (1 item in total) Kangi-in Seitendo |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/hakusho/html/hpab201301/1338525_019.pdf|format = PDF |page= 294|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2018-07-10}}</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 106 of July 9, 2012</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url= http://www.city.kumagaya.lg.jp/kanko/midokoro/menumasyoudenzan/kangiinkokuho.html |title=“Kangi-in Seitendo” designated as a national treasure|date= 2012-07-09|accessdate= 2012-07-12|publisher= Kumagaya City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|Japanese book|others= Cultural Properties Protection Committee; Agency for Cultural Affairs Cultural Properties Protection Department |title = Newly designated cultural properties |work= Monthly cultural properties |publisher = Daiichi Hoki Publishing |number= 586|year = 2012|issn= 0016-5948 |ncid= AN00221652}}</ref>.

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
[[File:Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|Shakujo head of Kangiin, Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|The statues of Kangiten and Two Doji are cast in the center. ]]
*Kisomon - An 18m high copper plate roofed eight-legged gate located at the front entrance of the temple grounds. This unique gate has a double roof, upper and lower, with two gable roofs at the front and back, and when viewed from the side, has three gables. Statues of Jikokuten and Tamonten are placed on the left and right. It was built by Masamichi Hayashi of Menuma in the 4th year of the Kaei era, and completed around 1855.
*Shakujoto - The secret principal image of Buddha in Shotendo. There is an inscription dating back to 1197, and the statues of Kangiten and Nidoji are cast in the center. A shakujo is a staff held by Jizo Bodhisattva and others, and the head of the staff sometimes represents a Buddha statue.
